title: Onshape Help
path: Welcome to Onshape Help
desc: Onshape's master help system, which contains help for all of the platforms that Onshape works on. To get started with Onshape we highly recommend going through the Primer first. This walks you through pertinent account preferences, how to begin a sketch, make a part, and other Onshape basics.

title: Getting Started with Onshape
path: Getting Started with Onshape
desc: To use Onshape efficiently (either on a browser, or in the app), here are some helpful things to know about its design, functionality, and user interface. Onshape runs in a browser, and mobile device apps exist for both iOS and Android. There is no software to download or maintain, ever. On a browser, Onshape updates automatically.

title: Hardware and Graphics Performance Recommendations
path: Getting Started with Onshape > Hardware and Graphics Recommendations
desc: This topic covers Hardware and graphics performance recommendations. To ensure optimal GPU performance when using Onshape, browse the recommendations here and compare to your configuration.

title: Graphics Area Display Data
path: Getting Started with Onshape > Hardware and Graphics Recommendations > Graphics Area Display Data
desc: This topic explains how display data refinement works in Onshape and what display data indicators are shown when a user navigates between tabs and in a Part Studio and Assembly tab.

title: Error Messages
path: Getting Started with Onshape > Hardware and Graphics Recommendations > Error Messages
desc: Onshape helps you identify errors and potential issues with error messages.

title: Performance Considerations
path: Getting Started with Onshape > Performance Considerations
desc: Part of any modeling process, in any tool, is modeling efficiently and appropriately for manufacturing, workflow, and yes, modeling itself. When you create models using CAD tools effectively, you reduce regeneration times for the entire model. In Onshape, there are specific steps you can take to ensure efficiency of modeling and reduced regeneration times.

title: Performance Panel
path: Getting Started with Onshape > Performance Considerations > Performance Panel
desc: The Performance panel provides statistics related to the model, graphics, and document, in addition to system details. These statistics can alert you to areas where the document, Part Studio and Assembly structure can be improved to obtain a more efficient performance.

title: AI Advisor
path: Getting Started with Onshape > AI Advisor
desc: An AI expert to answer your Onshape questions. Use the AI Advisor panel to ask a question to get information and references from Onshape's extensive resource library.

title: Explore Onshape
path: Getting Started with Onshape > Explore Onshape
desc: Explore Onshape through guided tutorials

title: Product Data Management (PDM) in Onshape
path: Getting Started with Onshape > Product Data Management (PDM) in Onshape
desc: Onshape brings both CAD and PDM capabilities together and centralizes these processes using a cloud-native approach. All PDM capabilities are fully integrated in the Onshape CAD platform, giving Engineers a seamless approach to maintaining your CAD and PDM systems in one place.

title: User Interface Basics
path: Getting Started with Onshape > User Interface Basics
desc: Visualization of toolbar locations, Part Studio interface and default settings.

title: Keyboard Shortcuts and Hotkeys
path: Getting Started with Onshape > User Interface Basics > Keyboard Shortcuts and Hotkeys
desc: To open the Keyboard shortcuts map in the user interface, Click the Help icon at the top right in the toolbar and select Keyboard shortcuts, or press Shift+/ on your keyboard.

title: Search Tools
path: Getting Started with Onshape > User Interface Basics > Search Tools
desc: Search for tools and custom features while using a Part Studio or Assembly.

title: Selection
path: Getting Started with Onshape > User Interface Basics > Selection
desc: Select parts or planes. Onshape selection works like a toggle. Click to select, click again to deselect. You are also able to click to additively select and deselect (the same behavior you would expect from Ctrl+click).

title: Create Selection
path: Getting Started with Onshape > User Interface Basics > Selection > Create Selection
desc: Onshape provides the Create selection dialog to make selecting related faces, such as faces that define a pocket on a model, easy. This is especially useful in certain commands, such as Delete face and Replace face. An alternative to Create selection is the Select command through the same context menu.

title: Select Other
shortcuts: ` (grave accent key, to the left of the “1” key)
path: Getting Started with Onshape > User Interface Basics > Selection > Select Other
desc: Use Select other to select entities (sketch curves, part faces, etc) that you might not be able to see in the graphics area because they are obscured by other entities.

title: Triad Manipulator
path: Getting Started with Onshape > User Interface Basics > Triad Manipulator
desc: Use the manipulator to move the part in any direction and angle in relation to the selected face(s) or edge(s) in Part Studio and Assembly.

title: Dialogs
path: Getting Started with Onshape > User Interface Basics > Dialogs
desc: Dialogs are used wherever user input is required.

title: Numeric Fields
path: Getting Started with Onshape > User Interface Basics > Numeric Fields
desc: Numeric measurements are required in multiple fields in Part Studio and Assembly. Numeric value fields throughout Onshape Part Studios and Assemblies accept integers, decimals, parameter expressions and trigonometric functions. Default units dictate the unit when no other unit is entered in the numeric field, but you can always enter any unit.

title: Context Menus
path: Getting Started with Onshape > User Interface Basics > Context Menus
desc: Context menus contain commands for that entity or workspace in the current context. Context menus exist for entities in the graphics area, Feature lists, Parts lists, Drawings, as well as Onshape constructs such as tabs. Right-click throughout the interface to discover context menus.

title: Colors
path: Getting Started with Onshape > User Interface Basics > Colors
desc: Onshape uses several colors to indicate what is selected or occurring in the Onshape application. This topic helps you understand how these colors are used.

title: Error Indicators
path: Getting Started with Onshape > User Interface Basics > Error Indicators
desc: Onshape helps you identify errors and potential issues with error indicators.

title: Printing
path: Getting Started with Onshape > User Interface Basics > Printing
desc: You can print (or download an image of) any Part Studio or Assembly in Onshape.

title: App Store
path: Getting Started with Onshape > App Store
desc: The App Store allows you to access third-party applications for use with Onshape.

title: App Store FAQs
path: Getting Started with Onshape > App Store > App Store FAQs
desc: Commonly asked questions about the Onshape App Store.

title: Documents
path: Documents
desc: Onshape has created a new document concept within the CAD industry. Instead of creating and working files, Onshape provides documents in which you can create, import and organize not just your CAD data, but also all supporting data and information that is pertinent to your CAD projects, such as parts, assemblies, drawings, imported data, images, and more. These types of data are stored in their own tabs within a document.

title: Document Tabs
path: Documents > Document Tabs
desc: Parts Studios, Assemblies, and non-native files imported into Onshape documents are represented in tabs in the user interface. Click a tab to select it and make it active. Only one tab is active in one browser tab at a time, but you can open any tab in a new browser tab to have multiple active tabs open. In addition to working in a tab, you can perform actions on tabs. Right-click on a tab to access the context menu for that tab.

title: Document Panel
path: Documents > Document Panel
desc: The Document panel is available in all Onshape documents (aligned vertically with the Onshape logo).

title: Document Toolbar
path: Documents > Document Toolbar
desc: The Document toolbar is available in all Onshape documents (aligned horizontally with the Onshape logo).

title: Document Menu
path: Documents > Document Menu
desc: The Document menu, located on the Document toolbar, contains commands related to the current document workspace or version.

title: Setting Default Units
path: Documents > Setting Default Units
desc: Onshape defaults to inch/degree for units of measure for all documents and workspaces. You can specify a different unit of measure in any numeric field and the value will be converted to the default unit automatically.

title: In-app Notifications
path: Documents > In-app Notifications
desc: In-app notifications appear under the bell icon in the Document toolbar and report on uploads, translations, exports, document upgrades, workflows, and more.

title: Documents Page
path: Documents > Documents Page
desc: The Documents page is the first page displayed when you sign in to your Onshape account. The exception is that Enterprise subscription users will land on the Activity page when you sign in. Click the Onshape logo (or your company logo) to return to the Documents page. This page lists all of the Onshape documents you have any permission to, including just view permission.

title: List View
path: Documents > Documents Page > List View
desc: List view, available to Enterprise and Professional plan subscribers, allows you to view the latest released and revisioned parts, Assemblies/subassemblies, and Drawings in each folder. Filter data in Onshape based on your product's structure. Data is presented in the same view, no matter how users in your company have structured their documents. Browse information naturally rather than having to know document naming conventions or how users have set up their documents.

title: Structure View
path: Documents > Documents Page > Structure View
desc: The Structure view is located on the Documents page. View the latest released and revisioned models and all associated parts and assemblies in a tree list, presenting the information from the top level assembly downward.

title: Create Menu
path: Documents > Documents Page > Create Menu
desc: From the Documents page, create documents, folders, publications, projects, and labels, in addition to importing files externally or from a cloud drive.

title: Folders
path: Documents > Documents Page > Folders
desc: Create folders for organizing documents and also for applying Share permissions on all documents with the folder and within any sub-folders. Note that all Share permissions on a folder are inherited by the documents and folders within that folder.

title: Labels
path: Documents > Documents Page > Labels
desc: Onshape provides a way for you to group and label documents to better organize them. You have the ability to label individual documents or groups of documents at a time. You also have the ability to relabel documents, apply more than one label to a document, remove a label from a document, and add and delete labels at will. All labels are user-specific, and no other user sees the labels you apply to documents, regardless of permissions.

title: Filters
path: Documents > Documents Page > Filters
desc: You have multiple options for organizing and then locating your data in Onshape. This section covers how to use Onshape filters and the available filter options.

title: Integrations
path: Documents > Documents Page > Integrations
desc: If you have previously integrated your Google Drive, Dropbox, and/or Microsoft OneDrive accounts into Onshape, the Integration appears above the Trash on your Documents page.

title: Advanced Search
path: Documents > Documents Page > Advanced Search
desc: An advanced search allows you to search for a Document, Part, Part Studio, Assembly, Publication, Drawing or other Onshape entity within the active filter.

title: Documents Page Panels
path: Documents > Documents Page > Panels
desc: Located on the right side of the Documents page, panels are where information for the selected document, folder, or publication is accessed.

title: Trash
path: Documents > Documents Page > Trash
desc: The Trash filter lists all documents that you have sent to trash (deleted). You see only those documents you have sent to trash. Any documents you delete from the trash, and all those present in trash when you click Empty Trash, are deleted forever. You can, however, right-click on any item in trash and Restore it.

title: Document Management
path: Documents > Document Management
desc: Onshape captures the state of every tab in a workspace every time an edit is completed (by all users working in that workspace). This information is also preserved for versions. For every document there is an infinite record of states in which it has existed. You never have to worry about constantly saving your work. Make changes with confidence and if the changes don't work out, you can find and restore any earlier state. Use version, branching, and merging to explore multiple design variations in parallel, either on your own or with collaborators.

title: Versioning and Branching
path: Documents > Document Management > Versions, Branches, and History
desc: You can create versions (which are View only) and branch a version to create a new workspace. You can also compare history entries in workspaces and versions, and any combination of the two. For more information, see Comparing.

title: Comparing
path: Documents > Document Management > Versions, Branches, and History > Comparing
desc: Onshape provides a mechanism for graphically and discretely comparing versions and workspaces at any history point. You are able to compare any combination: workspaces with workspaces or versions, versions with version or workspaces, and at any history entry if desired.

title: Repairing
path: Documents > Document Management > Versions, Branches, and History > Repairing
desc: Onshape provides a mechanism for graphically aiding repair of broken references at any history point: View in repair. In most cases, View in repair is initiated after editing a Derived or Import feature to a new base part, causing broken references in the Part Studio. This opens a repair panel to the right of the Part Studio to help guide you to where repairs are needed.

title: Merging
path: Documents > Document Management > Versions, Branches, and History > Merging
desc: Onshape provides a mechanism for merging from a document version or workspace (referred to as the Source) into your currently active document workspace (referred to as the Target). Specifically, when you merge a selected Source (workspace or version) into the currently active Target (workspace), all changes made in the Source are merged into the Target, including any additional features, tabs, etc.

title: Restoring
path: Documents > Document Management > Versions, Branches, and History > Restoring
desc: Onshape provides a mechanism for restoring from a previous point in a document branch (referred to as the Source) into the same branch (referred to as the Target).

title: Workspace Protections
path: Documents > Document Management > Versions, Branches, and History > Workspace Protections
desc: Onshape enables users to protect workspaces from unintentional design changes and to implement processes around how design changes are incorporated into important branches. When workspace protections are enabled, all changes to a document must be completed on a branch and then merged into the protected workspace.

title: Document Notes
path: Documents > Document Management > Document Notes
desc: Add text, Markdown, and hyperlinks into a Document notes panel.

title: Where Used
path: Documents > Document Management > Where Used
desc: The Where used command allows you to discover in which Assemblies and Drawings a particular part or assembly is being used, or in which document version a Feature Studio is being used. This is particularly helpful when you need to make a change to a part or assembly in production and need to understand the ramifications of that change.

title: Properties (Metadata)
path: Documents > Document Management > Properties (Metadata)
desc: Set metadata via the Properties dialog. You can set metadata for documents, parts, Part Studios, assemblies, drawings, and more. Set properties like name, description, part number, revision, state, and more, as well as any custom properties you or your company created. Any properties you set are shared for the entire company.

title: Publications
path: Publications
desc: Use Publications to create a collection of any released parts, Part Studios, Assemblies, Drawings, and files from any documents and share it with any user with an Onshape account.

title: Model Visualization Tools
path: Model Visualization Tools
desc: Model visualization tools are used to help view the model in specific ways in the graphics area, aiding you during model creation and during model analysis. Some of these tools include showing, hiding, and isolating model parts or instances, and making them transparent.

subsection: View Navigation and the View Cube
title: View Navigation and the View Cube
path: Model Visualization Tools > View Navigation and the View Cube
desc: Learn how to use Camera and render options to set up the model's view in the graphics area.

title: Mobile Touch Interface Navigation
path: Model Visualization Tools > Mobile Touch Interface Navigation
desc: Explore a series of videos that demonstrate the mobile touch interface, sketching, part design, and assemblies on mobile.

title: Camera and Render Options
path: Model Visualization Tools > Camera and Render Options
desc: Learn how to navigate in the Graphics area using your input device, and use Camera and render options to set up the model's view in the graphics area.

title: Isometric, Dimetric, and Trimetric Projections
availableIn: Part Studio, Assembly, Render Studio, PCB Studio
path: Model Visualization Tools > Camera and Render Options > Isometric, Dimetric, and Trimetric Projections
desc: Select from one of 3 projection methods to view the model in the graphics area: Isometric, Dimetric, and Trimetric. These Axonometric projections are used to represent 3D objects on a 2D plane, to simulate perspective.

title: Graphics Preferences
path: Model Visualization Tools > Camera and Render Options > Graphics Preferences
desc: Adjust visualization parameters of the model in the graphics area. Alter general viewport, shaded body, phantom edge, and mesh body parameters, as well as active/inactive sketch line width and colors, and construction line gap and dash lengths. These options are especially useful when modeling surfaces.

title: Named Views
path: Model Visualization Tools > Camera and Render Options > Named Views
desc: You have the ability to create and name views for use later within a workspace. Named views capture the perspective, the zoom scale, and the orientation of the current view.

title: Previous View
path: Model Visualization Tools > Camera and Render Options > Previous View
desc: Click the Previous view option in the Camera and render options dropdown to revert the model in the graphics area back to the view it was previously on.

title: Zoom to Fit, Window, and Selection
path: Model Visualization Tools > Camera and Render Options > Zoom to Fit, Window, and Selection
desc: Use Zoom to fit, Zoom to window, and Zoom to selection to adjust the view of the current model in the graphics area to fit the screen, selected bounding box, or selection, respectively.

title: Perspective View
path: Model Visualization Tools > Camera and Render Options > Perspective View
desc: Perspective view shows the relative distance from the point of view to the model, and creates a vanishing point as the point of view (or imaginary camera) approaches the model. The images below show a front view of the same part without perspective view and with perspective view, respectively.

title: Orient Normal to Sketch on Edit
path: Model Visualization Tools > Camera and Render Options > Orient Normal to Sketch Plane

title: Shaded, Unshaded, and Translucent
path: Model Visualization Tools > Camera and Render Options > Shaded, Unshaded, and Translucent
desc: Adjusts transparency/opacity of all parts and their edges in the graphics area.

title: Hidden Edges Visible and Removed
path: Model Visualization Tools > Camera and Render Options > Hidden Edges Visible and Removed
desc: Adjusts the visibility of all part edges that are obscured by other parts in the graphics area.

title: Tangent Edges Visible, Phantom, and Removed
path: Model Visualization Tools > Camera and Render Options > Tangent Edges Visible, Phantom, and Removed
desc: Tangent edges are edges formed between a curve and linear edge; for example, from fillets or smooth edges.

title: View in High Quality
path: Model Visualization Tools > Camera and Render Options > View in High Quality
desc: Toggle to select/deselect the highest available quality tessellation view for the currently active Part Studio or Assembly. Be aware that this may result in a slight degradation of performance.

title: Highlight Boundary Edges
path: Model Visualization Tools > Camera and Render Options > Highlight Boundary Edges
desc: Onshape displays holes and disconnects in a model, including laminar edges of surfaces, that may be in need of repair when you select Highlight boundary edges. This feature is especially helpful when importing parts that require repairing surfaces.

title: Section View
path: Model Visualization Tools > Camera and Render Options > Section View
desc: Section view allows for the selection of one or many planes, Mate connectors, cylindrical faces, conical faces, or planar faces to use for sectioning. Section view can be turned on through the Camera and render options menu, or by selecting Section view in the context menu.

title: Hide/Show
path: Model Visualization Tools > Hide/Show
desc: Hide/Show selected Part Studio or Assembly entities. These can be sketches, parts/instances, surfaces, mates, folders, or groups. Hide/Show are a set of toggle commands available from the context menu of a Parts list in a Part Studio, the Instances list in an Assembly, or the graphics area when hovering over a model.

title: Isolate
path: Model Visualization Tools > Isolate
desc: Isolate keeps all selected Part Studio or Assembly entities opaque, while making other entities transparent. Options include visualizing the transparent internal geometry so it can be selected, measured, analyzed, and edited, and expanding the isolated selection based on connectivity or physical proximity.

title: Make Transparent
path: Model Visualization Tools > Make Transparent
desc: Make selected Part Studio or Assembly entities transparent. Other entities remain opaque. Options include visualizing the transparent internal geometry so it can be selected, measured, analyzed, and edited, and expanding the transparent selection based on connectivity or physical proximity.

title: Viewing Models with Augmented Reality
path: Model Visualization Tools > Viewing Models with Augmented Reality
desc: Onshape enables viewing of models in a physical environment through the use of augmented reality. Place and view a model (part or assembly) in your physical space.

title: Viewing Models with AR View
path: Model Visualization Tools > Viewing Models with Augmented Reality > Viewing Models with AR View
desc: AR view is an Onshape feature enabling you to view models in a physical environment through the use of augmented reality. In this viewing mode, you can place and view a model (part or assembly) in your physical space.

title: Viewing Models with Apple Vision Pro
path: Model Visualization Tools > Viewing Models with Augmented Reality > Viewing Models with Apple Vision Pro
desc: Viewing models with Apple Vision Pro enables you to pair the Onshape iOS device to one ore more Apple Vision Pro devices via bluetooth over the same WiFi connection. The Onshape model (part, publication, or assembly) is then cast from the iOS device to the Apple Vision Pro devices using spatial computing.

title: Model Evaluation Tools
availableIn: Sketch, Part Studio, Assembly, Drawing (Measure tool only)
path: Model Evaluation Tools
desc: Model evaluation tools are a collection of tools used to measure, analyze, and display mass and section properties. They are located at the bottom right corner of the interface in Part Studios and Assemblies.

title: Measure Tool
path: Model Evaluation Tools > Measure Tool
desc: The Onshape Measure tool is available in Part Studios, assemblies, and drawings, for measuring sketches, parts, assemblies, curves, and surfaces. The Measure tool appears in the bottom right corner of the interface.

title: Analysis Tools
path: Model Evaluation Tools > Analysis Tools
desc: Analysis tools are used to inspect design integrity of sketch edges/surfaces and part edges/surfaces/volumes in Part Studios, and instance surfaces/interferences in Assemblies. The Analysis tools icon appears at the bottom right corner of the interface in Part Studios and Assemblies.

title: Curve/Surface Analysis
path: Model Evaluation Tools > Analysis Tools > Curve/Surface Analysis
desc: Curve/surface analysis visualizes and analyzes curvature using various methods on a sketch or part in a Part Studio. Access the Curve/surface analysis dialog box through shortcut keys (Shift+c), the context menu on a sketch, part, or surface, or through the Show analysis tools menu in the bottom right corner of the interface.

title: Deviation Analysis
path: Model Evaluation Tools > Analysis Tools > Deviation Analysis
desc: Display the minimum and maximum deviation between 2 curve chains in a Sketch or Part Studio, or 2 surfaces in a Part Studio.

title: Connection Analysis
path: Model Evaluation Tools > Analysis Tools > Connection Analysis
desc: Connection analysis assesses or reports the connection between curves and surfaces in a Sketch or Part Studio. Select two curves, faces, or any combination of the two, to analyze if the connection meets G0, G1, G2, and/or G3 continuity. Endpoints with multiple connections are not analyzed.

title: Dihedral Analysis
path: Model Evaluation Tools > Analysis Tools > Dihedral Analysis
desc: Dihedral analysis displays the dihedral angle of selected edges in Part Studios.

title: Interference Detection
path: Model Evaluation Tools > Analysis Tools > Interference Detection
desc: Interference detection detects and views any interference in a Part Studio or Assembly.

title: Zebra Stripes
path: Model Evaluation Tools > Analysis Tools > Zebra Stripes
desc: Zebra stripes represents the reflection of a striped room on the current model, faces, or surfaces in a Part Studio or Assembly. This allows you to see whether or not the curvature across edges is aligned and continuous.

title: Reflection Analysis
path: Model Evaluation Tools > Analysis Tools > Reflection Analysis
desc: Reflection analysis renders the model in the graphics area with a reflective material and environment image of your preference.

title: Curvature Color Map
path: Model Evaluation Tools > Analysis Tools > Curvature Color Map
desc: Curvature color map enables deeper investigation of curvature by applying a gradient of color of your choosing onto a face or surface in a Part Studio. You can adjust the scale of the color gradient and choose from different types of color maps to gain the best visual representation to discern surface continuity and transition between edges.

title: Draft Analysis
path: Model Evaluation Tools > Analysis Tools > Draft Analysis
desc: Draft analysis finds faces in the model that do not meet a specified minimum amount of draft, discovers undercut regions, and locates the potential parting line locations for selected geometries in a Part Studio.

title: Thickness Analysis
path: Model Evaluation Tools > Analysis Tools > Thickness Analysis
desc: Thickness analysis measures how much material is distributed throughout each region of a part. Currently, only native Onshape parts and mesh model types are supported. Closed composites are not currently supported.

title: Flatten Surfaces
path: Model Evaluation Tools > Analysis Tools > Flatten Surfaces
desc: Flatten surfaces generates a planar surface from one or more contiguous non-planar surfaces. The tool performs a geometric flattening to create a surface with minimum strain energy. The flattening operation ignores the material properties of the part on which the surface is flattened. The resultant surface has no material properties.

title: Mass Properties Tool
path: Model Evaluation Tools > Mass Properties Tool

title: Shared Modeling Concepts
path: Shared Modeling Concepts
desc: Shared modeling concepts include Onshape tools available across the product. These include modeling in context, configurations, imported CAD options, and mixed modeling.

title: Modeling In-Context
path: Shared Modeling Concepts > Modeling in Context
desc: Enables the user to select and edit a part in Part Studio in context to the other parts in the Assembly. Unselected parts cannot be edited in the Part Studio and appear transparent.

title: Configurations
path: Shared Modeling Concepts > Configurations
desc: Create variations of a part, Part Studio, assembly, or Variable Studio.

title: Part Studio and Assembly Configurations
path: Shared Modeling Concepts > Configurations > Part Studio and Assembly Configurations
desc: Create variations of a part, Part Studio, or assembly. For example, you can configure the depth of an extrude feature, the suppression of a fillet, the FeatureScript of a custom feature, part numbers, colors, materials, and more.

title: Variable Studio Configurations
path: Shared Modeling Concepts > Configurations > Variable Studio Configurations
desc: In Onshape, you can create your own configurations inside a Variable Studio.

title: Configured Properties
path: Shared Modeling Concepts > Configurations > Configured Properties
desc: You can configure properties (metadata) for each configuration input and option you define. You can configure part properties, appearance properties, and assembly properties. Administrators can also configure custom properties.

title: Managing Configurations
path: Shared Modeling Concepts > Configurations > Managing Configurations
desc: Rename, filter, copy, and paste configurations. Access context menus, set tolerance options, and work with dynamic suppression.

title: Visibility Conditions
path: Shared Modeling Concepts > Configurations > Visibility Conditions
desc: Add logic to your configurations to control when certain inputs and options are available.

title: Input Propagation
path: Shared Modeling Concepts > Configurations > Input propagation

title: Working with Imported CAD
path: Shared Modeling Concepts > Working with Imported CAD
desc: If you have existing CAD data in another system, you can import that data into Onshape and continue designing in Onshape. Onshape accepts data from many other systems, the most popular and well-translated being Parasolid files. This topic explains how to proceed and what tools are available after you've imported your existing CAD data into Onshape.

title: Mixed Modeling
path: Shared Modeling Concepts > Mixed Modeling
desc: Created mixed models by importing a mesh into an Onshape document, then modeling solid (analytical) bodies in relationship to that mesh. You can create assemblies using the mesh, the mixed model, and the analytical models.

title: Onshape Labs
path: Shared Modeling Concepts > Onshape Labs
desc: Onshape Labs is an innovation program for developing and testing next-generation capabilities, from AI-powered engineering assistants to breakthrough design workflows, directly within Onshape. It gives users early access to emerging features and a chance to help shape how they evolve.

title: FeatureScript Co-Complete
path: Shared Modeling Concepts > Onshape Labs > FeatureScript Co-Complete
desc: FeatureScript Co-Complete uses AI to contextually suggest and complete code as you type.

title: Descriptive Image Search
path: Shared Modeling Concepts > Onshape Labs > Descriptive Image Search
desc: Use AI to search images

title: Importing & Exporting Files
path: Importing & Exporting Files
desc: Import and export various file types, in addition to CAD files, from your hard drive and cloud based sources (such as Google Drive and Dropbox). When importing CAD files, Onshape automatically rewrites it to Onshape's internal format. When exporting files, you are able to export to another CAD format, as well as simply download non-CAD files.

title: Supported File Formats
path: Importing & Exporting Files > Supported File Formats
desc: A comprehensive list import and export file formats supported by Onshape. Onshape automatically imports and translates these CAD file formats for parts and assemblies, including wire bodies and sketch curves. For more on importing parts and assembly files see, Importing MCAD files.

title: Importing Files
path: Importing & Exporting Files > Importing Files
desc: You can import (upload) any type of file into Onshape, either into an existing and open document, or as its own document (from the Documents page). You can import files from your desktop and also from integrated Dropbox, Google Drive, or Microsoft OneDrive accounts.

title: Exporting Files
path: Importing & Exporting Files > Exporting Files
desc: Onshape enables you to export parts and surfaces (from Part Studios), entire Part Studios, entire Assemblies, as well as sketches and planar faces to your hard drive or cloud-source (for example, Google Drive or Dropbox) for use elsewhere.

title: Downloading Files
path: Importing & Exporting Files > Downloading Files
desc: Files that are unable to be processed upon export (primarily non-CAD files) are able to be downloaded through the Onshape tab context menu. You are able to download any tab that is able to be represented as a file.

title: Importing a Lidar Scan
path: Importing & Exporting Files > Importing a Lidar Scan
desc: Import a 3D scan of a space or object using a Lidar scanner integrated into an iOS device.

title: Sharing and Collaboration
path: Sharing and Collaboration
desc: Share a document with one or more users, enabling real-time collaboration right in the same document. Share with individuals, lists of individuals, teams, and companies, or make a document publicly available (or private again). You are also able to share the document with Onshape support, if needed.

title: Share Documents
path: Sharing and Collaboration > Share Documents
desc: Share a document to collaborate with other designers, change permission levels, or make a document publicly available. You are also able to share the document with Onshape Support, if needed.

title: Collaboration
path: Sharing and Collaboration > Collaboration
desc: Multiple users working in the same document at the same time is referred to as Simultaneous editing or Collaboration. Any and all features added or changes made are displayed in real time to all collaborators.

title: Commenting in Workspaces and Versions
path: Sharing and Collaboration > Comments in Workspaces and Versions
desc: Collaborating users have the ability to communicate with each other, in workspaces and versions, with comments and mentions. Owners of documents and those the document is shared with directly (and with Edit or Comment permission) have the ability to create comments, mention another user, see each others’ comments, leave replies, and opt to receive email notifications of comments.

title: Follow Mode
path: Sharing and Collaboration > Follow Mode
desc: When users are collaborating in a single document, they have the ability to choose to follow another collaborator. This allows the follower to see the actions of the other collaborator.

title: View Only Mode
path: Sharing and Collaboration > View Only Mode

title: Using the View Only Toolbar
path: Sharing and Collaboration > Using the View Only Toolbar
desc: The View Only toolbar is the default presentation for all users that do not have write permissions on a document.

title: Transfer Ownership
path: Sharing and Collaboration > Transfer Ownership
desc: Every document and folder is owned by either a user or a company. Users who belong to a company create company-owned documents and folders by default. Users who are not members of a company automatically own the documents and folders they create. For users belonging to more than one paid subscription, a drop down is included in the Create document/folder dialog with which you are able to select the owner at the time of creation.

title: Release Management
path: Release Management
desc: Release management is a set of automated workflows in Onshape used to manage releasing revisions of parts, assemblies, drawings and imported files (translated or not) in a document. This functionality is available only for the Onshape Professional and Enterprise subscriptions and allows you to establish workflows and tools for your entire company.

title: Setting Up Release Management
path: Release Management > Setting Up Release Management
desc: Only a company or Enterprise administrator is able to set up the details of the Onshape Release management workflow for the company, but any user in the account is able to use these tools in the company documents as long as they have edit permissions on the document (or documents) containing the objects for release.

title: Specifying Approvers
path: Release Management > Specifying Approvers
desc: By default, you are not required to list anyone as an approver on a release; the creator of a release may also be the approver. You are able to, of course, require an approver and also require that the approver must not be the creator, through the Release management settings under the Company/Enterprise settings page.

title: Typical Release Workflow
path: Release Management > Typical Release Workflow
desc: These instructions present the basic workflow of releasing any object, demonstrated with a single part.

subsection: Selecting Parts for a Release Candidate
title: Selecting Parts for a Release Candidate
path: Release Management > Selecting Parts for a Release Candidate
desc: Once a Release candidate has been created, you can include additional parts, Assemblies, Drawings, Variable Studios, or files from the document you are currently in that exist in the currently active workspace. Parts derived from another document in a Part Studio or linked from another document in an Assembly are included automatically in the Release candidate. Users (Enterprise only) can also add objects from another document to a release candidate.

title: Reviewing, Approving, Rejecting Candidates
path: Release Management > Reviewing, Approving, Rejecting Candidates
desc: When you create a Release candidate, you can require that it is reviewed and approved before being released by entering email addresses for a particular user or team of users in the Approver field. These users receive email notifications, and notifications within Onshape, containing links to view the Release.

title: Cloning a Release Package
path: Release Management > Cloning a Release Package
desc: Cloning a release package that has been released or rejected is an easy way to create a new release package once changes have been made to a part or parts within a workspace.

title: Viewing History and Obsoleting Parts
path: Release Management > Viewing History and Obsoleting Parts
desc: There are times in a Release process when you need to view the revision history of an object and there may also be times when you need to make an object obsolete.

title: Releasing a Configuration
path: Release Management > Releasing Configurations
desc: Onshape allows you to release configured parts and treats each configuration as a unique revisionable object.

title: PLM Connections
path: PLM Connections
desc: Product Lifecycle Management (PLM) Connections allow Onshape to send MCAD data to supported PLM solution providers.

title: The Onshape Arena Connection
path: PLM Connections > The Onshape Arena Connection
desc: This topic covers the basic workflow for setting up the connection so Onshape and Arena can successfully pass information between the two applications.

title: Configuring Arena and Onshape
path: PLM Connections > The Onshape Arena Connection > Configuring Arena and Onshape
desc: The target Arena Workspace for use with Onshape must be configured by Arena Support before a connection can be established with Onshape. Once that is done, you must configure your Onshape account to sign in and connect to your Arena account. This topic explains the steps for Administrators to take to ensure a proper connection can be made by establishing the correct configurations.

title: Syncing Parts, Assemblies, and BOMs
path: PLM Connections > The Onshape Arena Connection > Syncing Parts, Assemblies, and BOMs
desc: The Onshape Arena connection can be made without using the Release management workflow between Arena and Onshape. Syncing still occurs between Onshape and Arena items (parts, Assemblies and BOMs); however, an Onshape Release candidate is not synced to an Arena change. Both the Release candidate and Arena change move through their respective processes independent of each other.

title: Syncing Release Management
path: PLM Connections > The Onshape Arena Connection > Syncing Release Management
desc: Connecting Onshape's Release management workflow to Arena’s Change management system provides a unified Release/Change management solution for parts, Assemblies, and drawings created in Onshape. This approach guarantees that the Arena item revision always links to the Onshape part, Assembly, and drawing revision and version, allowing you to manage the iterative development and traceability of conceptual, pre-release, and production release designs.

title: Onshape Arena Glossary
path: PLM Connections > The Onshape Arena Connection > Onshape Arena Glossary
desc: Onshape glossary, providing definitions for key Onshape software terms. Covers terms in the context of the available connection between Onshape and Arena.

title: Part Studios
path: Part Studios
desc: This topic explains the functionality and mechanics of using Part Studios to create parts as well as how to customize the toolbars.

title: Customizing Appearance
path: Part Studios > Customizing Appearance
desc: Using the context menu for a specific part (or group of selected parts) you are able to customize not only the color of the part, but also assign materials (and thereby, a density) as well. When you need to control the tessellation (granularity of rendering of parts) for speed or accuracy, use this Appearance dialog also.

title: Feature and Part Lists
path: Part Studios > Features and Parts Lists
desc: The Part Studio Feature list consists of a list of features and a list of parts.

title: Customizing Part Materials
path: Part Studios > Customizing Part Materials
desc: Using the context menu for a specific part (or group of selected parts) you can customize not only the color of the part, but also assign a material (and thereby, a density), as well as specify a custom density without assigning a material. Onshape provides a material library for your use, and you are also able to add (or remove) your own custom material libraries.

title: Onshape Material Library
path: Part Studios > Customizing Part Materials > Onshape Material Library
desc: The Onshape material library content is created by Onshape, kept in documents within Onshape, and maintained by Onshape. There is never any risk of this content disappearing or not working from one release to another. We have integrated a time-saving process in this workflow to simplify applying common materials to parts.

title: Custom Tables
path: Part Studios > Custom Tables
desc: Custom tables allow you to view information from the current Part Studio, using FeatureScript custom tables. You can create the FeatureScript yourself (see Add Custom Features) and you can also sample community-created tables. Once a table is added to a Part Studio, it becomes available in all documents to which you have access.

title: Model-Based Definition (MBD)
path: Part Studios > Model-Based Definition (MBD)
desc: Model-based definition (MBD) refers to the process of dimensioning and annotating the model in the Part Studio so the model contain all the data needed to define a product, With MBD, the model becomes the source authority that drives all engineering activities. This model may further be used downstream by suppliers and across organizations within an enterprise.

title: Tolerance options
path: Part Studios > Model-Based Definition (MBD) > Tolerance Options
desc: Tolerances define the permissible range of values for a specified sketch dimension or Feature parameter, such as Extrude depth, Revolve angle, or Hole diameter. Not all sketch dimensions or Feature parameters can use tolerances.

title: Inspection table
path: Part Studios > Model-Based Definition (MBD) > Inspection table
desc: Inspect and add model based definitions to parts in the Part Studio. These include annotations like datums, dimensions, geometric tolerances, and weld symbols. Annotations can be set parallel or coincident with faces, and have annotation text aligned with faces or edges. The table can also be exported to a CSV file.

title: Onshape Default Tolerances Library
path: Part Studios > Model-Based Definition (MBD) > Onshape Default Tolerances Library
desc: The Onshape default tolerances library content is created by Onshape, kept in documents within Onshape, and maintained by Onshape. There is never any risk of this content disappearing or not working from one release to another. We have integrated a time-saving process in this workflow to simplify applying common default tolerances to parts.

title: Default Tolerances Library
path: Part Studios > Model-Based Definition (MBD) > Default Tolerances Library
desc: A default tolerances library is generally created by Administrators and used by Company users or teams to ensure tolerances adhere to tolerance defaults. Different Default tolerances can be created inside the library folder and used for specific purposes — for example, model evaluation or machining. Once created, users access the tolerances in the Inspection table in a Part Studio, as they model their parts.

title: Variable Table (Part Studio)
path: Part Studios > Variable Table (Part Studio)
desc: A Variable table allows you to create, view, and edit variable information in the current Part Studio or Assembly. Located on the right side of the graphics area with the Configuration panel, Appearance panel, and Custom tables, use the Variable table to create variables and change the value of a variable, even when the variable is used in a feature.

title: Hole Table
path: Part Studios > Hole Table
desc: View holes existing in the Part Studio, created through the use of the Hole tool in the Feature toolbar.

title: Surface modeling
path: Part Studios > Surface Modeling
desc: A surface is a single sided representation of a part's exterior that does not have a mass or thickness. Surface modeling is a modeling approach that allows designers to create complex geometric features and organic shapes that solid modeling tools cannot produce alone. Surface modeling is used for more free-form shapes and features than solid modeling.

title: Sketch Basics
path: Part Studios > Sketch Basics
desc: Use the Sketch toolbar to create a set of curves drawn on a plane, with a system of dimensions and constraints.

title: Sketch Tools
path: Part Studios > Sketch Tools
desc: Tools in the Sketch toolbar such as Line, Corner rectangle, Center point rectangle, Center point circle, 3 point circle, Tangent arc, 3 point arc, Spline, Point, and Construction used to create a sketch in a Part Studio.

title: Line
path: Part Studios > Sketch Tools > Line
desc: Sketch a line segment or series of line segments.

title: Midpoint Line
path: Part Studios > Sketch Tools > Midpoint Line
desc: Sketch a line starting symmetrically from its midpoint.

title: Corner Rectangle
path: Part Studios > Sketch Tools > Corner Rectangle
desc: Sketch a rectangle starting with a corner point.

title: Center Point Rectangle
path: Part Studios > Sketch Tools > Center Point Rectangle
desc: Sketch a rectangle starting with its center point.

title: Aligned Rectangle
path: Part Studios > Sketch Tools > Aligned Rectangle
desc: Sketch a rectangle, starting with a line and ending with the perpendicular distance of the aligned side.

title: Center Point Circle
path: Part Studios > Sketch Tools > Center Point Circle
desc: Sketch a circle starting with its center point.

title: 3 Point Circle
path: Part Studios > Sketch Tools > 3 Point Circle
desc: Sketch a circle by defining three points along its circumference.

title: Ellipse
path: Part Studios > Sketch Tools > Ellipse
desc: Sketch an ellipse by placing a center point and two axes radii (one major and one minor).

title: 3 Point Arc
path: Part Studios > Sketch Tools > 3 Point Arc
desc: Sketch an arc by defining the two end points and then the radius point.

title: Tangent Arc
path: Part Studios > Sketch Tools > Tangent Arc
desc: Sketch an arc at the end of a line.

title: Center Point Arc
path: Part Studios > Sketch Tools > Center Point Arc
desc: Sketch an arc by defining center, start, and end points.

title: Elliptical Arc
path: Part Studios > Sketch Tools > Elliptical Arc
desc: Sketch an elliptical arc by placing a temporary construction ellipse and then placing two points along the construction ellipse edge.

title: Conic
path: Part Studios > Sketch Tools > Conic
desc: Sketch an ellipse, parabola, or hyperbola by defining start, end, and control points, as well as a rho value.

title: Inscribed Polygon
path: Part Studios > Sketch Tools > Inscribed Polygon
desc: Sketch an inscribed polygon (polygon on the outside of the drawn circle).

title: Circumscribed Polygon
path: Part Studios > Sketch Tools > Circumscribed Polygon
desc: Sketch a circumscribed polygon (polygon on the inside of the construction circle).

title: Spline
path: Part Studios > Sketch Tools > Spline
desc: Sketch a multiple point curve with points along its length.

title: Bezier
path: Part Studios > Sketch Tools > Bezier
desc: Sketch a multiple point bezier curve with points along its length. The bezier curve follows the path of its control polygon.

title: Spline Point
path: Part Studios > Sketch Tools > Spline Control Point
desc: Add Spline control points along a spline or Bezier control polygon.

title: Point
path: Part Studios > Sketch Tools > Point
desc: Create points.

title: Text
path: Part Studios > Sketch Tools > Text
desc: Add up to 250 characters of text to a sketch (you are able to copy and paste into the text dialog). Treat sketch text as most other sketch entities: extrude, dimension, and apply constraints.

title: Use
path: Part Studios > Sketch Tools > Use
desc: Project (or convert) an edge, edges, and silhouette edges of a part or sketch onto the active sketch plane.

title: Intersection
path: Part Studios > Sketch Tools > Intersection
desc: Project (or convert) the intersection of a surface or face and the active sketch plane onto the sketch plane.

title: Construction
shortcuts: q (to toggle Construction state on and off)
path: Part Studios > Sketch Tools > Construction
desc: Sketch new construction geometry or convert existing geometry into construction geometry. Construction geometry are sketch entities used in creating other geometry but not used in creating features.

title: Sketch Chamfer
path: Part Studios > Sketch Tools > Sketch Chamfer
desc: Create bevels by setting the distance to break from the edge.

title: Sketch Fillet
path: Part Studios > Sketch Tools > Sketch Fillet
desc: Create fillets or rounds with a specified radius along one or more lines, arcs, or splines.

title: Trim
path: Part Studios > Sketch Tools > Trim
desc: Trim a curve to the first intersecting point or bounding geometry. If no intersection or bounding geometry is found, then the entire curve is deleted.

title: Extend
path: Part Studios > Sketch Tools > Extend
desc: Extend a line to the first intersecting point or bounding geometry. If no intersection or bounding geometry is found, then the line ends at the release point.

title: Sketch Split
path: Part Studios > Sketch Tools > Sketch Split
desc: Split open or closed sketch curves into multiple segments. Open curves require one or more points to split with; closed curves require two or more points.

title: Offset
path: Part Studios > Sketch Tools > Offset
desc: Offset the selected curve or loop at a specified distance and direction from the original.

title: Slot
path: Part Studios > Sketch Tools > Slot
desc: Create a slot around selected sketch curves (including splines, lines, arcs, chains of curves, and closed profiles).

title: Sketch Mirror
path: Part Studios > Sketch Tools > Sketch Mirror
desc: Create the reflection of one or more selected sketch entities about a specified line.

title: Sketch Pattern
path: Part Studios > Sketch Tools > Linear Sketch Pattern
desc: Create multiple instances of sketch entities uniformly in one or two directions.

title: Circular Sketch Pattern
path: Part Studios > Sketch Tools > Circular Sketch Pattern
desc: Create multiple instances of sketch entities uniformly about an axis or Mate connector. Circular patterns may be open or closed.

title: Transform Sketch
path: Part Studios > Sketch Tools > Transform Sketch
desc: Transform adjusts a sketch's location, orientation, and scale.

title: Insert DXF or DWG
path: Part Studios > Sketch Tools > Insert DXF or DWG
desc: Insert DXF or DWG files into a sketch as sketch entities. The DXF or DWG must have already been imported into the currently open document (or another document you own or that has been shared with you, creating a link to that document). It is recommended that you insert DXF or DWG files into an empty sketch, though it is possible to insert into a sketch with existing sketch entities.

title: Insert Image
path: Part Studios > Sketch Tools > Insert Image
desc: Use an imported image as a basis for a sketch. Upload an image to your document, then open that image in a sketch. Create sketch geometry using the image as a guide. Supported image types include: PNG, JPEG, and BMP.

title: Dimension
path: Part Studios > Sketch Tools > Dimension
desc: Add horizontal, vertical, shortest distance, angular, diametrical, arc length, or radial dimensions to sketch geometry, as well as between sketch geometry and planes. You are able to specify dimensions as driven (reference) or driving.

title: Coincident
path: Part Studios > Sketch Tools > Coincident
desc: Make two or more entities coincident, including a sketch entity and a plane.

title: Concentric
path: Part Studios > Sketch Tools > Concentric
desc: Make any point coincident with the center of an arc or circle by sharing a center point.

title: Parallel
path: Part Studios > Sketch Tools > Parallel
desc: Make two or more lines parallel.

title: Tangent
path: Part Studios > Sketch Tools > Tangent
desc: Form a tangent relation between two curves, or between a curve and a plane.

title: Horizontal
path: Part Studios > Sketch Tools > Horizontal
desc: Make one or more lines, or sets of points, align horizontally.

title: Vertical
path: Part Studios > Sketch Tools > Vertical
desc: Make one or more lines, or sets of points, align vertically.

title: Perpendicular
path: Part Studios > Sketch Tools > Perpendicular
desc: Form a right angle between two lines.

title: Equal
path: Part Studios > Sketch Tools > Equal
desc: Make multiple lines equal in length, or multiple arcs equal in radii.

title: Midpoint
path: Part Studios > Sketch Tools > Midpoint
desc: Constrain a point to the midpoint of a line or arc.

title: Normal
path: Part Studios > Sketch Tools > Normal
desc: Make a line and curve, or a curve and a plane normal to each other.

title: Pierce
path: Part Studios > Sketch Tools > Pierce
desc: Constrain a sketch entity (point or curve) to be coincident with the intersection point of its sketch plane and an arbitrary curve that is not in its sketch plane. The sketch entity is now constrained to be coincident with the point of intersection.

title: Symmetric
path: Part Studios > Sketch Tools > Symmetric
desc: Constrain two geometries (of the same type) to be symmetric relative to a line.

title: Fix
path: Part Studios > Sketch Tools > Fix
desc: Ground a sketch entity on the sketch plane so that it does not move.

title: Curvature
path: Part Studios > Sketch Tools > Curvature
desc: Create curvature continuous transitions between sketch splines (and conics) and surrounding geometry.

title: Flow
path: Part Studios > Sketch Tools > Flow
desc: Create flow continuous transitions (G3) between sketch splines (and conics) and surrounding geometry. Position, tangency, curvature, and the rate of change of curvature all match where the curves join.

title: Automatic Inferencing
path: Part Studios > Sketch Tools > Automatic Inferencing
desc: The Onshape sketch editor has the ability to assign constraints to certain entities automatically. For example, create a line and hover one of the endpoints above the origin and a dotted line appears indicating a vertical inference between that endpoint and the origin. When sketching, Onshape displays inferences for Horizontal and Vertical alignment between an entity and the origin and/or another entity. Some commonly used wake up inferences are: horizontal, vertical, midpoint, parallel, and coincident.

title: Working with Constraints
path: Part Studios > Sketch Tools > Working with Constraints
desc: Constraints are available and viewable when a sketch is being created or otherwise open for editing. Constraints applied between entities in two sketches (for instance, when you Use an entity from one sketch in another sketch) are differentiated by a blue background. Constraints may be applied manually and some are created when geometry is created as you sketch.

title: Troubleshooting Sketch Geometry
path: Part Studios > Sketch Tools > Troubleshooting Sketch Geometry
desc: This topic covers ways to troubleshoot sketch geometry. Onshape uses colors to indicate if a sketch is underconstrained, overconstrained, or fully constrained. Entities of an overconstrained sketch are red. Entities of an underconstrained sketch are blue. And entities of a fully constrained sketch are black.

title: Feature Basics
path: Part Studios > Feature Basics
desc: Many of our tools are 'combination' tools and serve many purposes like creating new material, adding additional material, removing material, and also creating intersecting material. This topic walks you through the basics of feature tool dialogs: how to use them, what the color paradigm means, and the other unique characteristics that make Onshape features easy to use.

title: Feature Tools
path: Part Studios > Feature Tools
desc: Feature tools create, modify, or manipulate 3-dimensional geometry to create new parts, modify existing ones, or generate construction tools for later use.

title: Extrude
path: Part Studios > Feature Tools > Extrude
desc: Add depth to a selected region or planar face along a straight path. Create a new part or surface or modify an existing one by adding or removing material, or intersecting parts in its path. Use Extrude to create parts, surfaces, or thin extrudes.

title: Revolve
path: Part Studios > Feature Tools > Revolve
desc: Create, add to, subtract from, or intersect parts by revolving sketch regions or planar faces about a central axis, or surfaces by revolving lines and curves about a central axis.

title: Sweep
path: Part Studios > Feature Tools > Sweep
desc: Define a shape using a selected region, curves, or planar face moving along a path (either solid or surface). Create a new part or modify an existing one by adding or removing material, or intersecting parts in its path.

title: Loft
path: Part Studios > Feature Tools > Loft
desc: Use profiles (sketch regions or sketch curves) and optional guide curves to define shapes that smoothly transition between them. Create parts or surfaces or modify existing parts or surfaces.

title: Thicken
path: Part Studios > Feature Tools > Thicken
desc: Add depth to a surface. Create a new part or modify an existing one by giving thickness to a surface and converting it to a solid, adding or removing material from an existing part or surface, or intersecting parts in its path.

title: Enclose
path: Part Studios > Feature Tools > Enclose
desc: Create a part by selecting all boundaries surrounding an empty space to form a solid. Use any set of surfaces and solids (including planes and faces) that intersect each other or connect at a boundary to create a volume. Create a new part or modify an existing one by adding, removing, or intersecting parts.

title: Fillet
path: Part Studios > Feature Tools > Fillet
desc: Round sharp interior and exterior edges and define as a standard constant radius, more stylized conic, or variable by selecting Edge fillet. Optionally apply a Full round fillet to create a seamless blend of one or more faces between two opposing sides.

title: Face Blend
path: Part Studios > Feature Tools > Face Blend
desc: Round sharp connected or disconnected interior and exterior faces to create a seamless blend between the faces or detach the blend to create new faces, defining a radius or constant width. Further define the blend cross section (rolling ball or swept profile), symmetry, control, trim, constraints, and limits.

title: Chamfer
path: Part Studios > Feature Tools > Chamfer
desc: Break sharp edges with a bevel. Define by the distance to break from the edge and by the angle made with the surface.

title: Draft
path: Part Studios > Feature Tools > Draft
desc: Apply a draft angle to one or more selected faces, or a parting line, in order to facilitate pulling a part from a mold.

title: Body Draft
path: Part Studios > Feature Tools > Body Draft
desc: Apply a draft angle to one or more selected parts using a parting surface and a pull direction.

title: Rib
path: Part Studios > Feature Tools > Rib
desc: Create ribs in parts at multiple locations based on a sketch.

title: Shell
path: Part Studios > Feature Tools > Shell
desc: Remove material from a part to produce a cavity of constant wall thickness with the option to remove zero faces (hollow) to many faces of the part (shell).

title: Hole
path: Part Studios > Feature Tools > Hole
desc: Create simple, countersink, and counterbore holes at sketch points, circle centers, and Mate connectors.

title: External Thread
path: Part Studios > Feature Tools > External Thread
desc: Create ANSI and ISO standard threads on convex cylindrical faces, like shafts and bolts. Threads appear as dashed lines at the top of the cylindrical face in drawings.

title: Linear Pattern
path: Part Studios > Feature Tools > Linear Pattern
desc: Replicate selected parts, faces, or features and arrange them in a row or grid pattern. Create new parts or modify existing parts by adding or removing material, or intersecting parts in its path. For information on creating circular patterns, see Circular Pattern. Linear pattern may also be used during an active sheet metal operation.

title: Circular Pattern
path: Part Studios > Feature Tools > Circular Pattern
desc: Replicate selected parts, faces, or features about an axis or Mate connector (inferred or existing). Create new parts or modify existing parts by adding or removing material, or intersecting parts in its path. For information on creating linear patterns, see Linear Pattern. Circular pattern may also be used during an active sheet metal operation.

title: Curve Pattern
path: Part Studios > Feature Tools > Curve Pattern
desc: Replicate selected parts, faces, or features along a sketch curve (or series of adjacent curves, edges on solid parts, and edges on wire parts) in the order of selection. Create new parts or modify existing parts by adding or removing material, or intersecting parts in its path. Curve pattern may also be used during an active sheet metal operation.

title: Mirror
path: Part Studios > Feature Tools > Mirror
desc: Replicate one or more selected parts or surfaces about a specified plane or planar face. Create a new part or surface or modify an existing one by adding or removing material, or intersecting parts in its path. Mirror may also be used during an active sheet metal operation.

title: Boolean
path: Part Studios > Feature Tools > Boolean
desc: Modify parts by merging parts or surfaces together (Union), removing a part/surface from a target (Subtract), or calculating the intersection between two or more parts or surfaces (Intersect).

title: Split
path: Part Studios > Feature Tools > Split
desc: Separate an existing part or face into multiple new parts or faces using a plane, Mate connector, surface or face of a part.

title: Transform
path: Part Studios > Feature Tools > Transform
desc: Adjust a part's (and its Mate connector or axis, if desired) location and orientation in 3D space with the option to copy the part in place. When transforming a part, you also have the ability to select its Mate connector (inferred or existing), or axis, so the Mate connector stays with the part.

title: Wrap
path: Part Studios > Feature Tools > Wrap
desc: Wrap a surface or sketch entity around a cylinder.

title: Decal
path: Part Studios > Feature Tools > Decal
desc: Place an image decal on a planar surface or cylinder.

title: Delete Part
path: Part Studios > Feature Tools > Delete Part
desc: Delete one or more parts or surfaces; this is a parametric operation that creates a delete-part feature and is able to be undone.

title: Modify Fillet
path: Part Studios > Feature Tools > Modify Fillet
desc: Alter or remove existing fillets or rounds; this Direct Editing tool is especially convenient if you don't have the parametric history of the part, as is often the case with an imported part.

title: Delete Face
path: Part Studios > Feature Tools > Delete Face
desc: Remove geometry from a part. Select whether to heal the surrounding faces (by extending until they intersect), cap the void, or leave the void open. This Direct Editing tool is especially convenient if you don't have the parametric history of the part, as is often the case with an imported part.

title: Move Face
path: Part Studios > Feature Tools > Move Face
desc: Translate, rotate, or offset one or more selected faces. This Direct Editing tool is especially convenient if you don't have the parametric history of the part, as is often the case with an imported part.

title: Replace Face
path: Part Studios > Feature Tools > Replace Face
desc: Trim a face or extend a face to a new surface. This Direct Editing tool is especially convenient if you don't have the parametric history of the part, as is often the case with an imported part.

title: Offset Surface
path: Part Studios > Feature Tools > Offset Surface
desc: Create a new surface by offsetting an existing face, surface, or sketch region. Set offset distance to 0 to create a copy in place.

title: Boundary Surface
path: Part Studios > Feature Tools > Boundary Surface
desc: Create or add a surface specified by its boundary profiles. Boundary Surface uses sets of curves from each direction (the U and V direction) to form a four-sided, closed surface with options to specify boundary conditions; for example, tangency matching and normal to profile.

title: Fill
path: Part Studios > Feature Tools > Fill
desc: Create a surface (or a part from surfaces) by defining boundaries and refine the surface with boundary conditions (instead of requiring the use of reference surfaces).

title: Move Boundary
path: Part Studios > Feature Tools > Move Boundary
desc: Move boundary edges of a surface in order to extend or trim it.

title: Ruled Surface
path: Part Studios > Feature Tools > Ruled Surface
desc: Create a ruled surface from an existing edge, sketch line, or curve. The ruled surface is defined by a series of lines between connecting points along the selected edge(s).

title: Mutual Trim
path: Part Studios > Feature Tools > Mutual Trim
desc: Trim two adjacent contiguous sets of surfaces by extending intersections to complete the trim. Each surface set can be flipped to select which side is kept, and all surfaces can be merged into a single surface or unmerged to keep all trimmed surfaces.

title: Constrained Surface
path: Part Studios > Feature Tools > Constrained Surface
desc: Create a surface from a selection of points or mesh data within a specified tolerance. Display deviations and optimize for performance or smoothness.

title: Plane
path: Part Studios > Feature Tools > Plane
desc: Create a new construction plane.

title: Helix
path: Part Studios > Feature Tools > Helix
desc: Create a helix using a conical or cylindrical face, axis object, or circular edge.

title: Projected Curve
path: Part Studios > Feature Tools > Projected Curve
desc: Create a Curve as the intersection of two projected sketches. Note that the projections from one sketch must intersect the other in one contiguous curve for this operation to succeed. The resulting Curve feature is listed in the Feature list and the curve itself is listed in the Parts list (when selecting a curve, use the Parts list).

title: 3D Fit Spline
path: Part Studios > Feature Tools > 3D Fit Spline
desc: Create a 3D fit spline through a series of vertices. Creates a curve which is listed in the Parts list under Curves.

title: Bridging Curve
path: Part Studios > Feature Tools > Bridging Curve
desc: Create a Curve connecting any two points, vertices, or Mate connectors. The resulting Curve is listed in the Feature list and the Parts list.

title: Composite Curve
path: Part Studios > Feature Tools > Composite Curve
desc: Represent multiple edges as one Curve. Select multiple adjacent edges, sketch entities, and other curves. Selecting non-contiguous edges may result in multiple Curves created. Selections for each Curve must meet at their vertices. (Curves are listed in the Parts > Curves list.)

title: Intersection Curve
path: Part Studios > Feature Tools > Intersection Curve
desc: Create a curve at the intersection at 2 or more surfaces or faces. The selections must intersect.

title: Trim Curve
path: Part Studios > Feature Tools > Trim Curve
desc: Trim or extend a curve by a distance or to a bounding entity.

title: Isocline
path: Part Studios > Feature Tools > Isocline
desc: Create an Isocline on a sloped face. The resulting Isocline is listed in the Feature list and Parts list.

title: Offset Curve
path: Part Studios > Feature Tools > Offset Curve
desc: Create and extend and/or split a new curve by offsetting edges on surrounding faces.

title: Isoparametric Curve
path: Part Studios > Feature Tools > Isoparametric Curve
desc: Create smooth curves that run along a face or surface in the U or V direction.

title: Edit Curve
path: Part Studios > Feature Tools > Edit Curve
desc: Edit an existing curve or create a new curve by selecting sketch entities or curves to apply a simplified approximation, elevate the degree, reposition control curve vertices, and/or planarize into any 2D plane.

title: Routing Curve
path: Part Studios > Feature Tools > Routing Curve
desc: Create a multi-point curve across one or more planes in 3D space (routed path). This is useful for creating pipe routing, wiring, and NURBS curves for advanced surfacing.

title: Mate Connector
path: Part Studios > Feature Tools > Mate Connector
desc: Mate connectors are local coordinate system entities located on or between sketches, parts, curves, or surfaces. They are used within a mate to locate and orient sketch, part, curve, or surface instances with respect to each other. You can also use Mate connectors to create planes.

title: Derived
path: Part Studios > Feature Tools > Derived
desc: Insert Part Studios, parts, surfaces, curves, sketches, planes, active sheet metal models, or mate connectors from one Part Studio into another in the same or a different document (thereby linking the documents), with an associative link. You also have the ability to insert these entities into a Part Studio from a different version of the same document.

title: Variable
path: Part Studios > Feature Tools > Variable
desc: Create a variable for use in expressions in a Part Studio, and assign a value. Use the variable in dimensions and expressions. Variables are features in Onshape, so the placement in the Feature list is important. Create a variable before the feature in which you will use it or create it on the fly during an operation that needs the value.

title: Query Variable
path: Part Studios > Feature Tools > Query Variable
desc: Create a selection group for use in expressions in a Part Studio. Use query the variable in dimensions and expressions. Query variables are features in Onshape, so the placement in the Feature list is important. Create a query variable before the feature in which you will use it or create it on the fly during an operation that needs the value.

title: Composite Part
path: Part Studios > Feature Tools > Composite Part
desc: A part comprised of selected bodies (parts, surfaces, curves, and/or points) grouped together to act as one part. You can create a closed composite part (one which consumes the bodies involved) or an open composite part (one that does not consume the bodies involved).

title: Tag
path: Part Studios > Feature Tools > Tag
desc: Tag sketch profile entities for use in Frames, parts to add or remove from Sheet metal forms, PCB holes for metadata used in PCB Studio board exports and imports, and parts to include in a custom standard content library. Select geometry, define orientation, and add properties.

title: Frame
path: Part Studios > Feature Tools > Frame
desc: Create a collection of swept bodies sharing a profile, arranged end-to-end.

title: Onshape Frame Profiles Library
path: Part Studios > Feature Tools > Frame > Onshape Frame Profiles Library
desc: The Onshape frame profiles library content is created by Onshape, kept in documents within Onshape and maintained by Onshape. There is never any risk of this content disappearing or not working from one release to another. We have integrated time-saving process in this workflow to simplify the insertion of frame profiles.

title: Frame Trim
path: Part Studios > Feature Tools > Frame Trim
desc: Create a collection of swept bodies sharing a profile, arranged end-to-end.

title: Gusset
path: Part Studios > Feature Tools > Gusset
desc: Create a collection of swept bodies sharing a profile, arranged end-to-end.

title: End cap
path: Part Studios > Feature Tools > End cap
desc: Create one or more end caps for frame segments.

title: Cut List
path: Part Studios > Feature Tools > Cut List
desc: Create a Frame, that is a collection of swept bodies sharing a profile, arranged end-to-end.

title: Sheet Metal Model
path: Part Studios > Feature Tools > Sheet Metal Model
desc: Create sheet metal parts by converting existing parts, extruding sketch curves (including arcs and splines to create rolled sheet metal), or thickening faces or sketches.

title: Sheet Metal Flange
path: Part Studios > Feature Tools > Sheet Metal Flange
desc: Create a wall for each edge selected for a sheet metal model, connected by a bend.

title: Sheet Metal Hem
path: Part Studios > Feature Tools > Sheet Metal Hem
desc: Create one or more hems on existing sheet metal parts.

title: Sheet Metal Tab
path: Part Studios > Feature Tools > Sheet Metal Tab
desc: Add a tab to a sheet metal flange, remove interfering material if appropriate, or bridge two flanges from the same sheet metal model. Sheet metal tabs are reflected in the model and in the flat pattern.

title: Sheet Metal Bend
path: Part Studios > Feature Tools > Sheet Metal Bend
desc: Bend a sheet metal model along a reference line, with additional bend control options.

title: Sheet Metal Jog
path: Part Studios > Feature Tools > Sheet Metal Jog
desc: Bend a sheet metal model along a reference line, with additional bend control options.

title: Sheet Metal Form
path: Part Studios > Feature Tools > Sheet Metal Form
desc: Create form features on existing sheet metal models. Forms can be selected from the current document, other documents, or a predefined library of sheet metal forms.

title: Sheet Metal Form Library
path: Part Studios > Feature Tools > Sheet Metal Form > Onshape Sheet Metal Forms Library
desc: The Onshape sheet metal forms library content is created by Onshape, kept in documents within Onshape and maintained by Onshape. There is never any risk of this content disappearing or not working from one release to another. We have integrated time-saving process in this workflow to simplify the insertion of forms.

title: Sheet Metal Loft
path: Part Studios > Feature Tools > Sheet Metal Loft
desc: Create a sheet metal part that transitions between two profiles.

title: Sheet Metal Make Joint
path: Part Studios > Feature Tools > Sheet Metal Make Joint
desc: Join or extend existing sheet metal walls into a bend or rip (that is displayed in the Bend/Rip table), creating associativity between the two edges. You have the ability to configure and further define the style of the bend or rip once it is created. To modify an existing joint, use Modify joint.

title: Sheet Metal Corner
path: Part Studios > Feature Tools > Sheet Metal Corner
desc: Modify a corner on a sheet metal model by selecting an edge, vertex, or face of the existing corner.

title: Sheet Metal Bend Relief
path: Part Studios > Feature Tools > Sheet Metal Bend Relief
desc: Modify a bend relief (the small cut made where the bend end meets a free edge), and by specifying a shape, and either a depth and relief width scale, or specific bend relief depth. You are also able to select to extend the bend relief in the opposite direction in the case of a flange, for example.

title: Sheet Metal Modify Joint
path: Part Studios > Feature Tools > Sheet Metal Modify Joint
desc: Editing an existing sheet metal model’s bends, rips, and joints using the Sheet metal table creates a Modify joint feature in the Feature list. Edit this feature as you would any other; right-click the feature entry to access the context menu.

title: Sheet Metal Corner Break
path: Part Studios > Feature Tools > Sheet Metal Corner Break
desc: Break the corner on existing sheet metal parts by applying a fillet or chamfer. Select a corner edge or vertex and specify corner break type and distance. It is recommended to use this feature after all flanges and joints of the Sheet metal model are finalized.

title: Sheet Metal Table and Flat View
path: Part Studios > Feature Tools > Sheet Metal Table and Flat View
desc: Edit an existing sheet metal model’s bends, rips, and joints. View the sheet metal flat pattern.

title: Finish Sheet Metal Model
path: Part Studios > Feature Tools > Finish Sheet Metal Model
desc: This tool deactivates one or more selected sheet metal models and causes them to be treated like any non-sheet metal solid parts. This allows you to perform post-fabrication operations on them, such as drilling at an angle through a face, welding corners, and adding form features and custom FeatureScript features.

title: Flex PCB Model
path: Part Studios > Feature Tools > Flex PCB Model
