desc: Create flexible PCB parts by converting existing parts, extruding sketches, or thickening faces or sketches. Operations on PCB models are automatically represented as a flat pattern, and joints and bends are listed in a table.

title: Finish Flex PCB Model
path: Part Studios > Feature Tools > Finish Flex PCB Model
desc: Deactivates the selected flex PCB model and causes it to be treated like any non-flex PCB part. This allows the user to optionally perform post-finishing operations, and continue editing the part with non-PCB features.

title: Add Custom Features
path: Part Studios > Feature Tools > Add Custom Features
desc: Custom features (and custom tables) are written in a programming language called FeatureScript and are created in an Onshape tab called a Feature Studio. These custom features are able to be added to your Feature toolbar for use in documents to which you have write access. Custom tables are available immediately in the document in which they are created, and you can add them to any other document (from a version).

title: Assemblies
path: Assemblies
desc: An Onshape Assembly tab is where you define a hierarchical structure of part and subassembly instances of an Assembly. It is also where you define degrees of freedom and relations. You are able to have more than one Assembly tab in a document. One Assembly can instance another Assembly as a subassembly, and/or instance a part directly. You are able to instance parts from the same document or other documents to which you have permissions (and that are versioned).

title: Insert Parts and Assemblies
path: Assemblies > Insert Parts and Assemblies
desc: Insert Parts and Assemblies inserts instances of parts, assemblies, sketches and surfaces into the active Assembly. You can instance specific parts (released or unreleased), sketches and surfaces defined in a Part Studio (or the entire Part Studio), and assemblies defined in a different Assembly tab, as well as all of these things from other documents (linking documents).

title: Linking Documents
path: Assemblies > Insert Parts and Assemblies > Linking Documents
desc: You can insert a part or assembly from a version of one Onshape document into an assembly in another Onshape Document, thereby linking the documents. Moving a part from one document to another creates a link to that part in any Assembly in which the part is previously inserted. You can also insert a part or assembly from a different version of the same document.

title: Updating References
path: Assemblies > Updating References
desc: Onshape allows you to insert parts and assemblies from any document into any other document. We refer to this as linking documents since referencing a part or assembly that resides in one document from another document (or within different versions of the same document) creates a sort of virtual link between the two documents (or two versions of the same document).

title: Instances List
path: Assemblies > Instances List
desc: The Insatances list in an Assembly tab contains a list of all part Instances, Groups, Mate connectors, Mates, and Relations defined for the Assembly. Use the context menu to act on any of these entities.

title: Standard Content
path: Assemblies > Standard Content
desc: Onshape standard content is content created by Onshape, kept in a database in Onshape, and maintained by Onshape. Users can insert Standard content in their Assemblies. There is never any risk of this content disappearing or not working from one release to another. We have integrated time-saving process in this workflow to simplify the insertion of standard content.

title: Onshape Standard Content Library
path: Assemblies > Standard Content > Onshape Standard Content Library
desc: This lists all of the standard content Onshape provides for your convenience. If the standard content you require is listed here, you don't have to model it - you can simply use the Insert parts and assemblies dialog to select the standard content you need. Check back here often to see what is available, since Onshape updates this list often.

title: Custom Standard Content Libraries
path: Assemblies > Standard Content > Custom Standard Content Libraries
desc: Create your own Standard Content library for users to insert in their assemblies.

title: Bill of Materials
path: Assemblies > Bill of Materials (BOM)
desc: Use the Onshape Bill of Materials (BOM) functionality to automatically create a BOM from any workspace Assembly. You can insert parts and assemblies into an Assembly post-release, from an Onshape version, or assemble the parts and sub-assemblies and then release the Assembly all at once. For more information on Release management, see Release Management.

title: Working with the BOM Table
path: Assemblies > Bill of Materials (BOM) > Working with the BOM Table
desc: Perform several functions from the BOM table, such as inserting non-geometric items, generating next or missing part numbers, switching to a Part Studio or Assembly from an item, open a linked document, suppress/show parts or subassemblies, and export the table to a CSV file.

title: BOM Table formatting
path: Assemblies > Bill of Materials (BOM) > BOM Table Formatting
desc: Add, remove, move, and resize columns, and sort items in the BOM table.

title: BOM Table Templates
path: Assemblies > Bill of Materials (BOM) > BOM Table Templates
desc: Once you have edited the BOM format, you can save that as a template and use it.

title: Mate Connector
path: Assemblies > Mate Connector
desc: Mate connectors are local coordinate system entities located on or between entities and used within a Mate to locate and orient instances with respect to each other.

title: Mates
path: Assemblies > Mates
desc: Mates in Onshape are different than mates in old CAD systems. There is only one Onshape Mate between any two instances, and the movement (degrees of freedom) between those two instances is embedded in the Mate. Mates contain their own coordinate systems, so you ever only need to use one Mate to define the degrees of freedom between two entities.

title: Fastened Mate
path: Assemblies > Mates > Fastened Mate
desc: Mate two entities and remove all degrees of freedom between them.

title: Revolute Mate
path: Assemblies > Mates > Revolute Mate
desc: Mate two entities allowing rotational movement about the Z axis. (Rz).

title: Slider Mate
path: Assemblies > Mates > Slider Mate
desc: Mate two entities allowing translational movement along the Z axis. (Tz).

title: Planar Mate
path: Assemblies > Mates > Planar Mate
desc: Mate two entities allowing translational movement along the X axis and the Y axis, and rotational movement about the Z axis (Ty, Tx, Rz).

title: Cylindrical Mate
path: Assemblies > Mates > Cylindrical Mate
desc: Mate two entities allowing translational movement along the Z axis and rotational movement about the Z axis (Tz, Rz).

title: Pin Slot Mate
path: Assemblies > Mates > Pin Slot Mate
desc: Mate two entities allowing rotational movement about the Z axis and translational movement along the X axis. (Rz, Tx).

title: Ball Mate
path: Assemblies > Mates > Ball Mate
desc: Mate two entities allowing rotational movement about the X, Y and Z axis (Rx, Ry, Rz).

title: Parallel Mate
path: Assemblies > Mates > Parallel Mate
desc: Mate two entities allowing individual translational movement along any axis, and parallel rotation along any axis.

title: Tangent Mate
path: Assemblies > Mates > Tangent Mate
desc: Mate two entities tangent to the selected faces, edges, or vertices.

title: Width Mate
path: Assemblies > Mates > Width Mate
desc: Mate up to two tabs to constrain them symmetrically between two mate connectors. Allow translation and normal rotation on a slot's center plane. The first selection defines the item to be centered. The second selection defines the center plane.

title: Group
path: Assemblies > Group
desc: Use Group to fix the position of selected instances relative to one another within the assembly. It is very convenient when the instances were all modeled in the same Part Studio in the correct locations relative to one another. Group enables you to keep that relative positioning without having to create Mates.

title: Snap Mode
path: Assemblies > Snap Mode
desc: Automatically create a Mate when inserting an entity into an Assembly, using explicitly created Mate connectors on the entity being inserted. Also, drag one entity (by a Mate connector) to snap to a Mate connector on another entity. Both methods result in an open Mate dialog so you are able to fine tune the Mate type and alignment.

title: Show Mates
path: Assemblies > Show Mates Mode
desc: In this mode, you are able to hover over or select instances in the graphics area or Instances list to show the mates for that instance.

title: Replicate
path: Assemblies > Replicate
desc: Replicate takes a seed entity or entities as input, a bolt for instance, and locates geometry identical to that which the seed is mated to (based on an additional selection). The seed is then replicated and mated to that matching geometry.

title: Replace Instance
path: Assemblies > Replace Instance
desc: Replace instance allows you to replace selected or all instances of a part, surface, sketch, or subassembly within an assembly. Even if the replacement component is slightly different (for example, a derivative of the part), it will be inserted and all previously associated mates reapplied.

title: Assembly Linear Pattern
path: Assemblies > Assembly Linear Pattern
desc: Pattern selected entities and arrange them in a row pattern. For information on creating circular patterns, see Assembly Circular Pattern.

title: Assembly Circular Pattern
path: Assemblies > Assembly Circular Pattern
desc: Pattern selected entities about an axis. For information on creating linear patterns, see Assembly Linear Pattern.

title: Assembly Mirror
path: Assemblies > Assembly Mirror
desc: Create mirrored instances of a part, surface, or subassembly. Specify the mirror plane and select a mirror strategy.

title: Relations
path: Assemblies > Relations
desc: Use relations on mates to constrain degrees of freedom between mates.

title: Gear Relation
path: Assemblies > Relations > Gear Relation
desc: Relate two Mates with revolute degrees of freedom. The relation creates a constant ratio of angular rotation between the Mates. If either mated part is moved, the other will move rotationally.

title: Rack and Pinion Relation
path: Assemblies > Relations > Rack and Pinion Relation
desc: Relate a Mate with a rotational degree of freedom to a Mate with a linear degree of freedom.

title: Screw Relation
path: Assemblies > Relations > Screw Relation
desc: Constrain the rotational degree of freedom in one Cylindrical Mate to the translational degree of freedom in the same Cylindrical Mate.

title: Linear Relation
path: Assemblies > Relations > Linear Relation
desc: Constrain the linear motion between two Mates to change at a constant ratio. The first Mate will move linearly in one direction as the other Mate is moved linearly in one direction.

title: Named Positions
path: Assemblies > Named Positions
desc: Assign a name to a specific position (that is, the Mate degree of freedom values, and absolute transforms for instances with no Mates) of the assembly and switch to a particular named position easily at any time. Keep in mind that the Mate values are relative and are able to be satisfied even if both sides of the Mate have moved.

title: Display States
path: Assemblies > Display States
desc: Assign a name to a specific display state (that is, with certain parts, subassemblies, or mates hidden or in view) of the assembly and switch to a particular display state easily at any time.

title: Create Part Studio in Context
path: Assemblies > Create Part Studio in Context
desc: Create a new Part Studio in the context of an existing assembly; positioning the assembly specifically for use when modeling the part. The assembly appears in the Part Studio as context graphics to be used for reference.

title: Simulation
path: Assemblies > Simulation
desc: Simulation, available to Enterprise and Professional plan subscribers, is used to evaluate the stresses and displacements between externally-loaded instances in an Assembly, allowing you to examine how an assembly reflects the loads, materials, and boundary conditions found in real-world use.

title: Modal Simulation
path: Assemblies > Simulation > Modal Simulation
desc: Modal analysis, or more specifically, natural frequency analysis is used to provide information on the stiffness or mechanical resonance of an assembly structure. It is used by designers and engineers who require vibrational analysis within Onshape and is commonly used in industrial equipment, automotive, and aerospace industries, among others. Modal analysis is often required for subsequent dynamic analysis; for example, modal frequency response and modal transient analysis are used in safety calculations.

title: Asynchronous Simulation
path: Assemblies > Simulation > Asynchronous Simulation
desc: With Asynchronous Simulation, a user runs simulations independent of their active modeling session. Simulation results are permanently stored in a Results and history table in the Simulation panel. Simulation results display the status of all jobs in the queue, in progress, and completed.

title: Rigid Body
path: Assemblies > Simulation > Rigid Body
desc: Select bodies to be included in the Simulation while remaining non-deformable.

title: Exploded Views
path: Assemblies > Exploded Views
desc: Manually manipulate an assembly into an exploded view using the manipulator to drag components or groups of components from their current positions to a new position. The steps are recorded in the Exploded views panel, complete with the ability to reorder and otherwise edit the view.

title: Assembly Variable Table
path: Assemblies > Assembly Variable Table
desc: A Variable table allows you to create, view, and edit variable information in the current Part Studio or Assembly. The Variable table is located on the right side of the graphics area with the BOM table, Configuration panel, Exploded views, and Named positions. A Variable table is created in a document and the variables therein are immediately available for use in all Part Studios and Assemblies in that document workspace.

title: Drawings
path: Drawings
desc: You have the ability to create mechanical drawings from within Onshape Part Studios and Assemblies and also of entire Part Studios. All Onshape drawings are based on the .DWG file format (drawing database) and the .DXF file format (Drawing Interchange File) is also supported.

title: Drawing Basics
path: Drawings > Drawing Basics
desc: This section covers the basics of working with Drawings, including creating drawings, basic drawing workflow, and navigating within drawings.

title: Creating a Drawing
path: Drawings > Drawing Basics > Creating a Drawing
desc: When you create a drawing of a part, curve, or surface in a Part Studio, or in an Assembly, the drawing contains default views. You are also able to create an empty drawing using the menu in the lower left corner of the window and select Create Drawing.

title: Custom Templates
path: Drawings > Drawing Basics > Custom Templates
desc: Drawing templates are comprised of a drawing format that includes the title block, border, zones, properties and styles. Once defined, the drawing template is available for reuse when new Drawings are created. In addition to allowing the creation of custom templates from scratch, Onshape also provides a number of public drawing templates to use and customize.

title: Sheets
path: Drawings > Sheets
desc: An Onshape sheet is a page of a drawing which represents a single sheet of paper in a printed version of a drawing. View the sheets of a drawing and their contents with the Sheet flyout, located on the left side of the interface.

title: Styles
path: Drawings > Styles
desc: Drawing styles are a collection of visual settings you can apply to one or more dimensions, without having them affect all dimensions globally, as when they are edited in the Properties panel. Styles are located in a panel on the right side of the drawings area. Click the icon to open the panel, and click again to close the panel.

title: Drawing Properties
shortcuts: Right-click on an empty area in the drawing and select Drawing properties
path: Drawings > Properties
desc: Click the icon on the right side of the drawings area to open the Drawing properties panel. Use these settings to define the defaults for your drawing. Individual drawing entities may be changed separately, but these settings apply to all entities in a drawing as a default. Once you have your drawing properties set to your satisfaction, you can save the drawing and its settings as a template.

title: Drawing Properties - Units and Precision
path: Drawings > Properties > Units and Precision
desc: Edit the current drawing's Primary and Dual units, and Leading and trailing zeros. Change each option by clicking the drop down menu arrows on the right side of the menu and selecting an option.

title: Drawing Properties - Dimensions
path: Drawings > Properties > Dimensions
desc: Edit the current drawing's font, text height, color, text alignment, text gaps, geometry gaps, and more. Change each option by clicking the drop down menu arrows on the right side of the menu and selecting an option.

title: Drawing Properties - Annotations
path: Drawings > Properties > Annotations
desc: Edit the current drawing's font, text height, arrowhead length and type, and color of each annotation type in your drawing. Supply defaults for all annotations at once, or Notes, Callouts, Datums, Geometric tolerances, Surface finish symbols, Weld symbols, Hole callouts, and Bend notes (for sheet metal) separately.

title: Drawing Properties - Views
path: Drawings > Properties > Views
desc: Edit the current drawing's projection angle, the color and thickness of your drawing's visible edges, tangent edges, hidden edges, cutting lines, arrowheads, view labels and more.

title: Drawing Properties - Construction Geometry
path: Drawings > Properties > Construction Geometry
desc: Edit the color and thickness of the drawing's centerlines and centermarks, as well as the style, color, and thickness of the drawing's virtual sharps. Use the Part Studio sketches section to edit the format of sketches brought into the drawing.

title: Drawing Properties - Formats
path: Drawings > Properties > Formats
desc: These properties enable / disable selection of objects in a drawing's border frame, border zone, and title block. The default for a new drawing is Locked; you are not able to immediately select objects in the title block, border, or border zones.

title: Drawing Properties - Tables
path: Drawings > Properties > Tables
desc: Edit Bill of Material (BOM), custom, cut list, hole, revision, and other tables created in the current drawing.

title: Drawing Properties - Inspection
path: Drawings > Properties > Inspection
desc: Edit the appearance of inspection items in the current drawing.

title: MBD Status
path: Drawings > MBD Status
desc: The MBD status panel lists the inserted part's model-based definitions data (annotations and dimensions) not visible in the drawing. If any visible data is deleted from a drawing view, it is also displayed in this panel and can be shown again.

title: Views
path: Drawings > Views
desc: When you create a drawing from a part, curve, surface, or subassembly, you have the ability to create it without any views, by default, or with 4 standard views: top, front, right, and isometric. Typically, the projection of the views depends on the standard chosen: first angle projection for ISO standard and third angle projection for ANSI standard, you can also use a custom template and select the projection, or change the projection after the drawing is created.

title: Projected View
path: Drawings > Views > Projected View
desc: Create a new view by projecting (folding) out an existing view.

title: Auxiliary View
path: Drawings > Views > Auxiliary View
desc: Create an auxiliary view; an orthographic view that is folded out 90 degrees from a selected edge in the parent view (usually from a slanted edge). Alternatively, you can create a sketch line or centerline about which to orient the auxiliary view.

title: Drawing Section View
path: Drawings > Views > Section View
desc: Create a section view, jogged section view, or partial section view of an existing view (including a section view) by placing a cutting plane line (or lines) and specifying a direction and label.

title: Aligned Section View
path: Drawings > Views > Aligned Section View
desc: Create a section view in which some portions of the view have been cut on a plane not parallel to the view plane and those portions have been rotated onto the view plane. This view type is most commonly used on cylindrical parts with some symmetry but not fully symmetrical.

title: Broken-Out Section View
path: Drawings > Views > Broken-Out Section View
desc: Create a broken-out section view to cut away a portion of the model in a drawing view by defining a closed profile with the Spline tool.

title: Detail View
path: Drawings > Views > Detail View
desc: Use Detail view to select an area of an existing view to enlarge for more detail.

title: Break View
path: Drawings > Views > Break View
desc: Use Break view to shorten an existing view by trimming out a portion.

title: Crop View
path: Drawings > Views > Crop View
desc: To crop a view, sketch a circle, spline, or polygon around the area you wish to keep.

title: Drawing Flat Pattern View
path: Drawings > Views > Flat Pattern View
desc: A sheet metal flat pattern view can only be inserted from the Insert dialog. Once inserted from this dialog it can be placed into the sheet.

title: View Context Menu
path: Drawings > Views > View Context Menu
desc: Hover over any view and right-click the mouse to open a context menu on any view to access a list of command options for that view. These command options are listed below. Not all options listed here are available for every type of view.

title: Drawing Dimensions
path: Drawings > Dimensions
desc: Place a dimension on any type of curve in a drawing.

title: Drawing - Dimension
path: Drawings > Dimensions > Dimension
desc: Known as the smart dimension tool, this places several types of dimensions on a curve in a drawing. The type of curve selected determines the type of dimension that is placed.

title: Drawing - Chamfer Dimension
path: Drawings > Dimensions > Chamfer Dimension
desc: Place a note or dimension on a chamfered edge.

title: Drawing - Maximum or Minimum Dimension
path: Drawings > Dimensions > Maximum or Minimum Dimension
desc: Place a minimum or maximum dimension directly to any combination of arcs, circles and any other geometry type, excluding curves.

title: Drawing - 2 Point Linear Dimension
path: Drawings > Dimensions > 2 Point Linear Dimension
desc: Measure the distance between two points. Create horizontal, vertical, and rotated linear dimensions.

title: Drawing - Point to Line Dimension
path: Drawings > Dimensions > Point to Line Dimension
desc: Measure the distance between a point and a line. Create horizontal, vertical, and rotated linear dimensions.

title: Drawing - Line to Line Dimension
path: Drawings > Dimensions > Line to Line Dimension
desc: Create dimensions between parallel lines.

title: Drawing - Line to Line Angular Dimension
path: Drawings > Dimensions > Line to Line Angular Dimension
desc: Measure the interior angle between the two legs and the exterior angle formed by two lines.

title: Drawing - 3 Point Angular Dimension
path: Drawings > Dimensions > 3 Point Angular Dimension
desc: Measure an angle by selecting 3 points, including a vertex and two points on the legs.

title: Drawing - Arc Length Dimension
path: Drawings > Dimensions > Arc Length Dimension
desc: Measure the length of an arc.

title: Drawing - Radial Dimension
path: Drawings > Dimensions > Radial Dimension
desc: Measure the radial dimension of a circle, arc, or circular arc centermark.

title: Drawing - Diameter Dimension
path: Drawings > Dimensions > Diameter Dimension
desc: Measure the diameter of a circle, arc or circular arc centermark, including silhouette edges.

title: Drawing - Foreshorten Dimension
path: Drawings > Dimensions > Foreshorten Dimension
desc: Place a foreshorten dimension on a silhouette edge, or on a centerline and an arc or circle edge, to create a half-diameter dimension in a Drawing.

title: Drawing - Ordinate Dimension
path: Drawings > Dimensions > Ordinate Dimension
desc: Create ordinate dimensions (X, Y pairs) for a feature measured from a datum. Ordinate dimensions created as a group move together when one is moved.

title: Drawing - Hole/Thread Callout
path: Drawings > Dimensions > Hole/Thread Callout
desc: Apply a hole callout to a hole or thread, automatically inserting the metadata of the hole or thread.

title: Datum
path: Drawings > Datum
desc: Use Datum to create and place associative datum symbols to the drawing view on a surface that appears as a linear or circular edge to identify datum planes in the part.

title: Geometric Tolerances
path: Drawings > Geometric Tolerance
desc: Often associated with datum, use Geometric tolerance to create and place basic dimension notations in the drawing.

title: Surface Finish
path: Drawings > Surface Finish
desc: Place a surface finish symbol on the edge of a circular view or away from edges.

title: Weld Symbol
path: Drawings > Weld Symbol
desc: Place weld symbols on a drawing. Weld standards default to the standard specified for the drawing. To change the weld standard, access the drawing’s Properties flyout located on the right side of the page.

title: Edge Condition Symbol
path: Drawings > Edge Condition Symbol
desc: Place an edge condition symbol on a Drawing to show the acceptable state of an edge or corner created during machining.

title: Note
path: Drawings > Note
desc: Add single or multi-line text notes to any drawing, wherever you want, and use them to fill in the title blocks as well. You have the ability to define the size of the text box as well as format the text itself and optionally include a leader or many leaders. You also have the ability to rotate the orientation of the note and create additional leaders.

title: Callout (Balloon)
path: Drawings > Callout (Balloon)
desc: Create and edit callouts (balloons) with a leader line. Callouts are associative with the part metadata of the document and a BOM table when a BOM App is used within your Onshape document. When a BOM table is present, the callout defaults to use the Item Number in the table. If the table order is changed, use the Update Drawing feature to update the callouts.

title: Table
path: Drawings > Table
desc: Add fully-customizable tables to any drawing.

title: BOM Table
path: Drawings > BOM Table
desc: Insert a Bill of Materials table from an Onshape BOM table, uploaded file, or an authorized app. You are also able to use the Balloon tool to automatically pull identifiers from the BOM to label the drawing. See Balloon for more information.

title: Cut List Table
path: Drawings > Cut List Table
desc: Insert a Bill of Materials table from an Onshape BOM table, uploaded file, or an authorized app. You are also able to use the Balloon tool to automatically pull identifiers from the BOM to label the drawing. See Balloon for more information.

title: Hole Table
path: Drawings > Hole Table
desc: Insert a hole table for a view or multiple views of a common, singular part (and not an entire Part Studio). Style the table as you would any other table, and hover over a table row for cross-highlighting in the drawing.

title: Custom Table
path: Drawings > Custom Table
desc: Insert a custom table into a drawing. Custom tables tabulate Part Studio data. Updates to the Part Studio update the data in the custom table. See Updating a Drawing for more information.

title: Revision Table
path: Drawings > Revision Table
desc: Insert a revision table to record the revisions of the drawing created during the release management process. Style the table as you would any other table and adjust properties of the table through the Properties panel. As the drawing moves through the release management process, further revisions and table information are updated automatically.

title: Drawing Construction Tools
path: Drawings > Drawing Construction Tools
desc: Onshape provides tools for creating sheet geometry: drawing entities like lines and centerlines, created on the sheet outside of a view and meant to represent some part of the 3D model.

title: Drawing Sketch Tools
path: Drawings > Drawing Sketch Tools
desc: Onshape provides tools for creating sheet sketch geometry: drawing entities like lines, circles, and rectangles, created on the sheet.

title: Working with Drawing Constraints
path: Drawings > Working with Drawing Constraints
desc: Apply constraints between sketch entities and drawing view geometry.

title: Insert DXF or DWG
path: Drawings > Insert DXF or DWG
desc: Insert the contents of a DXF or DWG file as Onshape drawing entities. Use this tool as a method to create a custom template; for more information see Custom Drawing Templates.

title: Insert Image
path: Drawings > Insert Image
desc: You can insert and scale JPG, PNG, and GIF images on a drawing sheet, such as a logo and QR and bar codes.

title: Format Painter
path: Drawings > Format Painter
desc: Use the Styles panel format of one dimension or annotation to format additional dimensions or annotations in the drawing.

title: Inspection Item
path: Drawings > Inspection Item
desc: Add Inspection items to the drawing, on multiple sheets, numbered, and attached to the desired annotation or callout type, including: dimensions, tolerances (including for separate frames), surface symbols, notes, etc. Note that Inspection items cannot be attached to datums.

title: Updating a Drawing
path: Drawings > Updating a Drawing
desc: When an underlying Part Studio or Assembly of a drawing is changed, the drawing may need to be updated, as indicated by the active yellow icon (the inactive icon is grayed out). Changes that trigger this condition may be seemingly insignificant, like moving a sketch dimension or hiding a construction plane in a Part Studio. To understand better why this button is active, check the History of the document to view recent changes.

title: Dangling entities
path: Drawings > Updating a Drawing > Dangling Entities
desc: A dangling entity in a drawing is an entity that has lost one (or more) of its reference points. Dimensions, section lines, note leaders, callouts, centermarks, and geometric tolerances are all examples of entities that could become dangling (broken) after a drawing update. This is to be expected, especially if the change to the part or assembly was significant.

title: Importing a Drawing
path: Drawings > Importing a Drawing
desc: This section covers how to import Drawings. They can be imported from the Documents page where they automatically become a new document, or within a document, where they automatically become a tab inside that document.

title: Exporting a Drawing
path: Drawings > Exporting a Drawing
desc: You can export Onshape drawings to the following file types: PDF, DWG, DXF, DWT, SVG, PNG, JPEG, and CSV (for Drawing Inspection item lists). To set up Export rules for drawings, including exporting the inspection symbol count of a drawing, see how to set the preference in your account under Managing Your Onshape Plan.

title: Printing a Drawing
path: Drawings > Printing a Drawing
desc: This topic covers how to print Drawings.

title: Variable Studios
path: Variable Studios
desc: This topic explains the functionality and mechanics of using a Variable Studio to create variables that can be used in the document in which they are created as well in other documents.

title: Feature Studios
path: Feature Studios
desc: A Feature Studio is a tab containing FeatureScript, a programming language used to define your own custom features in Onshape.

title: Render Studios
path: Render Studios
desc: This Onshape Render Studio application, free for Enterprise and Professional plan subscribers, allows you to create photorealistic scenes from your imported Part Studios or Assemblies. Use scenes to test model appearances and materials, lighting and camera setups, and environments. Export scenes as .jpg- or .png-formatted images to market your rendered designs.

title: Render Studio Basics
path: Render Studios > Render Studio Basics
desc: This section explains Render Studio basic navigation and workflow.

title: Render Studio Interface
path: Render Studios > Render Studio Interface
desc: The sections below explain how each area of the Render Studio tab's interface works. You can create multiple Render Studio tabs, each containing a dashboard with a number of Render Studio scenes.

title: Render Studio Interface - Toolbar
path: Render Studios > Render Studio Interface > Toolbar
desc: Located at the top of the page, the toolbar contains several commands that are commonly performed when working in Render Studio.

title: Render Studio Interface - Scene List
path: Render Studios > Render Studio Interface > Scene List
desc: Located on the left side of the page, the Scene list provides part, Part Studio and Assembly information for the current Render Studio scene.

title: Render Studio Interface - Graphics Area
path: Render Studios > Render Studio Interface > Graphics Area
desc: The Graphics area is where the scene is visually located. It appears in the center of the Render Studio application.

title: Render Studio Interface - Appearances Library
path: Render Studios > Render Studio Interface > Appearances Library
desc: Located at the bottom of the page, the Appearances library contains all the standard attribute combinations that are applied to parts, part faces, or surfaces, to provide a material texture, as well as functions that are applied to appearance parameters.

title: Appearance Functions
path: Render Studios > Render Studio Interface > Appearances Library > Appearance Functions
desc: Functions are a special type of appearance that perform a specific action on a part's appearance parameter. When a scene is created, every part has a default set of appearance parameters, viewable in the Appearance panel on the right.

title: Appearance Modifiers
path: Render Studios > Render Studio Interface > Appearances Library > Appearance Modifiers
desc: Modifiers are a special type of appearance that are used to modify other appearances. These modifiers do not overwrite the prior appearance. Instead, the modifier is associated to the Base material parameter of the new modifier appearance.

title: Textures and Bump Maps
path: Render Studios > Render Studio Interface > Appearances Library > Textures and Bump Maps
desc: Apply textures, custom image textures, bump textures, and custom bump textures to a part's appearance parameters in Render Studio.

title: Light Emission
path: Render Studios > Render Studio Interface > Appearances Library > Light Emission
desc: There are several appearances devoted to adding and emitting light from a part, surface, or face in a scene. Which light appearance is used depends on the light source and how the scene in question should be lighted.

title: Render Studio Interface - Environments Library
path: Render Studios > Render Studio Interface > Environments Library
desc: Located at the bottom of the page, the Environments library contains all the standard environments that are added as the backdrop for the Part Studio, Assembly, and parts in the scene. An environment also provides scene illumination.

title: Render Studio Interface - Appearance Panel
path: Render Studios > Render Studio Interface > Appearance Panel
desc: Located at the right of the page, the Appearance panel displays an editable list of parameters for the appearance of the selected object. The Appearance is material-specific (for example, Fabric, Glass, or Masonry), and the available panel parameters change, depending on the selected Appearance.

title: Render Studio Interface - Environment Panel
path: Render Studios > Render Studio Interface > Environment Panel
desc: Located at the right of the page, the Environment panel displays an editable list of parameters for the scene environment. The available panel parameters change, depending on the selected Environment. Click the Environment panel icon to open the panel.

title: Render Studio Interface - Camera Panel
path: Render Studios > Render Studio Interface > Camera Panel
desc: Located at the right of the page, the Camera panel displays an editable list of parameters for the Camera directed at the selected object, such as Field of view, Focal length, Position, Rotation, Background, Depth of Field, Exposure, Tone and contrast, Vignetting, and other Advanced options.

title: Render Studio Interface - Scene Panel
path: Render Studios > Render Studio Interface > Scene Panel
desc: Located at the right of the page, the Scene panel displays an editable list of global parameters for the Scene list. Click the Scene panel icon to open the panel.

title: Render Studio Interface - Render Options
path: Render Studios > Render Studio Interface > Render Options
desc: Render options determine how the scene is output to a JPEG or PNG image file. Once scene edits are completed, click the Render scene button on the toolbar to open the Render options dialog.

title: Render Studio Advanced
path: Render Studios > Render Studio Advanced
desc: Render Studio Advanced provides additional functionality when working in Render Studio tabs.

title: AxF Appearance (Render Studio Advanced)
path: Render Studios > Render Studio Advanced > AxF Appearance
desc: X-rite AxF appearances are a self-contained file format which are output by X-rite scanning devices such as the TAC-7, MA-T12 and MetaVue VS3200. Unlike a texture file these files completely describe an appearances properties and may include both uniform and spatially varying information.

title: Appearance Set (Render Studio Advanced)
path: Render Studios > Render Studio Advanced > Appearance Set
desc: The Appearance set is an Appearance modifier that is assigned to an entity (Part Studio, Assembly, part, face). Once assigned, multiple appearances can be added to the set in the Appearance panel. Switching between appearances in the set provides a quick and easy method to experiment with appearance variations.

title: Volume (Render Studio Advanced)
path: Render Studios > Render Studio Advanced > Volume
desc: A volume is a cubic region in which the volumetric portion of an appearance exists and is rendered. The volume can optionally be an OpenVDB 3D texture. Non-advanced users can open a scene that contains Volumes, but their properties are non-editable.

title: Light (Render Studio Advanced)
path: Render Studios > Render Studio Advanced > Light
desc: A Light is a Render Studio Advanced scene entity that creates an explicit source of luminescence, with position and direction. Light is emitted into the scene based on one of 3 distribution types (Diffuse, Spot, and Profile) that determines how light varies with the angle to the light source. Lights may also have a surface area that cause them to cast softer shadows.

title: Render Studio Examples and Resources
path: Render Studios > Render Studio Examples and Resources
desc: This topic includes additional examples and resources to get the most out of the Render Studio application.

title: Render Studio Libraries
path: Render Studios > Render Studio Libraries
desc: This topic provides tables that outline the standard Render Studio Appearances and Environments libraries and their descriptions.

title: PCB Studio
path: PCB Studios
desc: This Onshape PCB Studios application, free for Enterprise and Professional plan subscribers, allows you to create models using ECAD files for reference. PCB Studios helps you create shapes for printed circuit boards using Onshape, export those models created in Onshape in an IDF format and send them to an electrical engineer to use to create PCB designs in an ECAD system.

title: Altium 365 Integration
path: PCB Studios > Altium 365 Integration
desc: Altium 365 Integration links a user's Altium account to their Onshape account. Once integrated, the user can browse Altium workspaces, and import Altium boards directly into PCB Studio without the need to use files. When an Altium board is imported, it can be created in Onshape using the same tools already used for boards imported from file formats like IDF.

title: Rigid-Flex PCB
path: PCB Studios > Rigid-Flex PCB
desc: Import Rigid-flex PCBs into Onshape from Altium 365 or an IDX file, or create Rigid-flex PCBs in Onshape that can be exported to an IDX file.

title: CAM Studios
path: CAM Studios
desc: Onshape CAM Studios allow you to create cutting strategies, or toolpaths, based off of CAD model geometry. The strategies are posted into a language that a CNC machine interprets called Gcode. The CNC machine uses this code to manipulate the machine axes and cutting tools to remove material from a piece of stock as a form of subtractive manufacturing.

title: Account Menu
path: Account Menu
desc: The Account menu, located under your name in the upper-right corner of the interface, allows you to access My account, Action items, View support tickets, Switch to. . . , Company or Enterprise settings, and Sign out.

title: My Account Settings
shortcuts: Shortcut toolbars - Customize the shortcut toolbars available for Sketch tools, Feature tools, Assembly tools, and Drawing tools.
path: Account Menu > My Account Settings
desc: My account settings is where you can manage and maintain your Onshape account, set preferences, notifications settings, security and all the account settings, as explained in this topic. See blow for more information.

title: My Account - Profile
path: Account Menu > My Account Settings > Profile
desc: The Onshape user profile displays general information about you and your account, such as Name, username, nickname, bio, and documentation name.

title: My Account - Emails
path: Account Menu > My Account Settings > Emails
desc: Displays email settings. Add, remove, or edit your primary or other emails.

title: My Account - Preferences
path: Account Menu > My Account Settings > Preferences
desc: Displays preference settings for your account, such as language, startup page, units, mouse controls, toolbars, keyboard shortcuts, and more.

title: Export Rule Conventions
path: Account Menu > My Account Settings > Preferences > Export Rule Conventions
desc: Some default Onshape properties, and all custom properties, can be used as export rule conventions.

title: My Account - Notifications
path: Account Menu > My Account Settings > Notifications
desc: Displays email and mobile notifications settings for shares and comments.

title: My Account - Security
path: Account Menu > My Account Settings > Security
desc: Displays security settings, where you can reset your password.

title: My Account - Devices
path: Account Menu > My Account Settings > Devices
desc: Displays devices settings, where you can create device profiles for use with Onshape.

title: My Account - Applications
path: Account Menu > My Account Settings > Applications
desc: Displays applications settings, where you can add or remove the applications you use with your Onshape account.

title: My Account - Integrations
path: Account Menu > My Account Settings > Integrations
desc: Displays the integrations settings, where you can grant Onshape access to your Dropbox, Google Drive, or Microsoft OneDrive account (separately).

title: My Account - Developer
path: Account Menu > My Account Settings > Developer
desc: Allow users to create api keys for managing apps.

title: My Account - Early Visibility
path: Account Menu > My Account Settings > Early Visibility
desc: Displays the early visibility settings, where you can manage access to the Onshape early visibility program, allowing you to test functionality that is under development.

title: My Account - Subscription
path: Account Menu > My Account Settings > Subscriptions
desc: Displays subscription settings, where you can view, edit, update, or cancel your subscription.

title: My Account - Payment Options
path: Account Menu > My Account Settings > Payment Option
desc: Displays payment option settings, where you can edit credit card and billing information.

title: My Account - Payment History
path: Account Menu > My Account Settings > Payment History
desc: Displays your payment history. Only Company account Owners and Administrators can see this information for Professional plans. Users in Standard and Free plans can see their history (in case a Free user has downgraded from another plan).

title: My Account - Teams
path: Account Menu > My Account Settings > Teams
desc: Displays team settings, where you can add or remove teams.

title: Action Items
path: Account Menu > Action Items
desc: Action items are a sortable list of tasks that can be assigned by you or to you by another user within your Company/Enterprise. They can be release tasks or comments and can have the status of open or closed. Action items show up on the Enterprise tab bar at the top of the Onshape application.

title: Company/Classroom/Enterprise Settings
path: Account Menu > Company/Classroom/Enterprise Settings
desc: View the account setting for your company (Company settings), Classroom (Classroom settings), or enterprise (Enterprise settings).

title: Company/Classroom/Enterprise Settings - Users
path: Account Menu > Company/Classroom/Enterprise Settings > Users
desc: Invite or add new users to your company/classroom/enterprise, view the list of current users, search for a particular user, delete selected users, and see whether a user is a Guest user. Only the company/classroom/enterprise Owner and the Admin (or Educator in the case of Classrooms) have the ability to add users to and remove users from the subscription.

title: Company/Classroom/Enterprise Settings - Teams
path: Account Menu > Company/Classroom/Enterprise Settings > Teams
desc: Create teams of users to group users together for the purpose of making sharing more efficient; once the team is created, you can select the team name instead of entering many users' individual email addresses during a Share operation. All team members must be users in the company/classroom/enterprise.

title: Enterprise Settings - Aliases
path: Account Menu > Company/Classroom/Enterprise Settings > Aliases
desc: Aliases are distribution lists for the Release management workflow. Only Administrators can create Aliases and assign other users or Teams to an alias. Specifically, an Administrator needs the Manage users and teams global permission in order to create aliases and assign other users or teams to an Alias.

title: Enterprise Settings - Global Permissions
path: Account Menu > Company/Classroom/Enterprise Settings > Global Permissions
desc: Global permissions control user access to Enterprise-level operations and information. Only the enterprise administrator or another user with administrator rights can grant Global permissions to users. The user who creates the Enterprise account becomes the first administrator of the account and is assigned the Enterprise administrator global permission.

title: Enterprise settings - Connections
path: Account Menu > Company/Classroom/Enterprise Settings > Connections
desc: Establish a connection to share data between an outside enterprise to one or more users in your enterprise. Data is not shared with your entire enterprise, only users you specify.

title: Enterprise Settings - Authentication
path: Account Menu > Company/Classroom/Enterprise Settings > Authentication
desc: Configure and manage two-factor authentication (2FA), single sign on (SSO), and domain verification.

title: Enterprise Settings - Project Roles
path: Account Menu > Company/Classroom/Enterprise Settings > Project Roles
desc: Project roles are used to group users into functional roles with associated permissions. For example, you may have Project roles like Designer, Engineer, Reviewer, and Vendor. These roles act as buckets that you will later group specific users into when you’re creating a Project.

title: Enterprise Settings - Permission Schemes
path: Account Menu > Company/Classroom/Enterprise Settings > Permission Schemes
desc: Project roles and Permission schemes work in tandem to apply access permission to documents grouped together within a Project. A Project references only one Permission scheme, which is comprised of Project roles specifying the permissions. Permission schemes are a named table of Role-Permission set pairs.

title: Company/Classroom/Enterprise Settings - Properties/Custom Properties
path: Account Menu > Company/Classroom/Enterprise Settings > Properties/Custom Properties
desc: Access the metadata definitions for Onshape objects (what drives the data displayed in object Properties dialogs and Bill of materials (BOM)), view these metadata definitions, and create new properties for use in Company/Classroom/Enterprise-owned documents, as well as provide Display names for existing Onshape properties. Administrators can add, modify and retire properties for all users. Users can only view these metadata definitions.

title: Company/Classroom/Enterprise Settings - Categories
path: Account Menu > Company/Classroom/Enterprise Settings > Categories
desc: Create categories in Onshape to extend the properties of the standard Onshape object types in the system to include more targeted and relevant metadata to be applied based on design, engineering, and manufacturing processes.

title: Company/Classroom/Enterprise Settings - Items
path: Account Menu > Company/Classroom/Enterprise Settings > Items
desc: Add items that you will want to add to your bill of materials but that do not require being modeled (non-geometric entities). Adding those items here allows you to make use of them in any company/enterprise-owned documents.

title: Company/Classroom/Enterprise Settings - Applications
path: Account Menu > Company/Classroom/Enterprise Settings > Applications
desc: Access and manage third-party applications for use with your Onshape Professional, Educator, or Enterprise subscription.

title: Company/Classroom/Enterprise Settings - Numbering Schemes
path: Account Menu > Company/Classroom/Enterprise Settings > Numbering Schemes
desc: Select manual or sequential number generation for release objects (parts, Assemblies, drawings, files), standard content, and items.

title: Company/Classroom/Enterprise Settings - Release Management
path: Account Menu > Company/Classroom/Enterprise Settings > Release Management
desc: Select from a set of automated workflows in Onshape used to manage releasing revisions of parts, Assemblies, Drawings and imported files (translated or not) in a document.

title: Enterprise Settings - Task Management
path: Account Menu > Company/Classroom/Enterprise Settings > Task Management
desc: Allows Enterprise admins to manage task workflows. Enterprise admins can activate, deactivate, unpublish, and set default task workflows for the Enterprise.

title: Company/Classroom/Enterprise Settings - Preferences
path: Account Menu > Company/Classroom/Enterprise Settings > Preferences
desc: Select your Onshape Preferences settings, where you have the ability to require that users use approved drawing templates, make use of company/classroom/enterprise-owned material libraries in their own accounts, or show a view only toolbar to all users of a document with view only permissions, as well as additional preference settings.

title: Company/Classroom/Enterprise Settings - Revision Tools
path: Account Menu > Company/Classroom/Enterprise Settings > Revision Tools
desc: Change the part number type of released objects to allow for part number reuse bewteen types (i.e., parts, assemblies, and drawings).

title: Enterprise Settings - Integrations
path: Account Menu > Company/Classroom/Enterprise Settings > Integrations
desc: Available to Enterprise administrators only; grant or remove access to Cloud storage integrations and integration users, and set up Collaboration integrations, such as Slack.

title: Company/Classroom/Enterprise Settings - Webhooks
path: Account Menu > Company/Classroom/Enterprise Settings > Webhooks
desc: Administrators can use webhooks to check data access integrity, ensuring that a notification was really sent by Onshape, and that it has not been tampered with in transit. Enabling webhook basic authentication populates the Authorization header in all webhook requests.

title: Company/Classroom/Enterprise Settings - Developer
path: Account Menu > Company/Classroom/Enterprise Settings > Developer
desc: Allow Enterprise admins to create new apps to which Enterprise users can subscribe. Admins can manage and distribute these apps to specified users.

title: Enterprise Settings - Arena
path: Account Menu > Company/Classroom/Enterprise Settings > Arena
desc: Grant or remove access to Microsoft OneDrive, Dropbox, and Google Drive accounts to Onshape.

title: Enterprise Settings - Job Queue
path: Account Menu > Company/Classroom/Enterprise Settings > Job Queue
desc: Provides a list of all Arena PLM BOM and Release candidate sync jobs and their statuses.

title: Company/Classroom/Enterprise Settings - Details
path: Account Menu > Company/Classroom/Enterprise Settings > Details
desc: View and update the details of the company/classroom/enterprise information and change the logo image.

title: Account Menu
path: Account Menu > Inactive Onshape Account Policy
desc: An inactive Onshape account is an account that has not been used (logged into) during the past 4 years. Inactive accounts are deleted after 4.5 years.

section: Managing Your Onshape Account and Subscription
title: Managing Your Onshape Account And Subscription
path: Managing Your Onshape Account and Subscription
desc: Onshape offers different types of accounts based on different levels of need regarding data management and collaboration requirements: Enterprise, Professional, Standard, Education, and Free.

section: Managing Your Onshape Account and Subscription
title: Subscriptions and Payment FAQs
path: Managing Your Onshape Account and Subscription > Subscriptions and Payment FAQs
desc: This topic covers Plan Faq, outlining subscriptions and payment questions and answers.

section: Managing Your Onshape Account and Subscription
title: Free Account
path: Managing Your Onshape Account and Subscription > Free Subscription
desc: This topic covers how to manage your Onshape free subscription.

section: Managing Your Onshape Account and Subscription
title: Student Subscription
path: Managing Your Onshape Account and Subscription > Student Subscription
desc: Student subscriptions are for degree- or certificate-seeking students at accredited education institutions. This plan is solely for classroom instruction, student learning projects, school clubs or organizations, and academic research. This plan is not for government, commercial, or other organizational use.

section: Managing Your Onshape Account and Subscription
title: Standard Subscription
path: Managing Your Onshape Account and Subscription > Standard Subscription
desc: Standard subscriptions are directed towards single professional users who do not have a need for company-wide settings and functionality. Standard subscriptions are billed per user (at an annual rate of $1,500), and include all Onshape features with the exception of the following: Automated Release management tools, Custom properties (company metadata), Company-wide material libraries, Company-based sharing, and Consolidated billing.

section: Managing Your Onshape Account and Subscription
title: Managing Your Onshape Professional Trial
path: Managing Your Onshape Account and Subscription > Professional Trial
desc: A Professional Trial, available from a Free or Standard subscription, allows you to try out all the features of a Professional subscription, and then transition to a Professional subscription once the trial is over.

section: Managing Your Onshape Account and Subscription
title: Professional Subscription
path: Managing Your Onshape Account and Subscription > Professional Subscription
desc: The Onshape Professional subscription enables you to consolidate billing for multiple users, thereby creating a Company within Onshape: a named, user-visible Onshape entity with consolidated billing, ownership and sharing for a set of Professional subscription users.

section: Managing Your Onshape Account and Subscription
title: Managing Your Onshape Educator Subscription
path: Managing Your Onshape Account and Subscription > Educator/EDU Enterprise Subscription
desc: Educator subscriptions are for current faculty members or volunteers at accredited education institutions, and provides access to Classes and Assignments. This plan is solely for classroom instruction, organizations, and academic research. This plan is not for government, commercial, or other organizational use.

section: Managing Your Onshape Account and Subscription
title: Educator Concepts and Terminology
path: Managing Your Onshape Account and Subscription > Educator/EDU Enterprise Subscription > Educator/EDU Enterprise Concepts and Terminology
desc: This topic covers the terms and concepts to help provide a foundation for understanding and using Onshape Educator subscription.

section: Managing Your Onshape Account and Subscription
title: Educator Interface
path: Managing Your Onshape Account and Subscription > Educator/EDU Enterprise Subscription > Educator/EDU Enterprise Interface
desc: This topic explains the Educator user interface.

section: Managing Your Onshape Account and Subscription
title: Educator Classes
path: Managing Your Onshape Account and Subscription > Educator/EDU Enterprise Subscription > Educator/EDU Enterprise Classes
desc: This topic explains how to administer Educator classes.

section: Managing Your Onshape Account and Subscription
title: Educator Assignments
path: Managing Your Onshape Account and Subscription > Educator/EDU Enterprise Subscription > Educator/EDU Enterprise Assignments
desc: This topic explains how to administer Educator assignments.

section: Managing Your Onshape Account and Subscription
title: EDU Enterprise Dashboards
path: Managing Your Onshape Account and Subscription > Educator/EDU Enterprise Subscription > EDU Enterprise Dashboards
desc: Available dashboards in the EDU Enterprise plan and the information contained therein.

section: Managing Your Onshape Account and Subscription
title: Enterprise Subscription
path: Managing Your Onshape Account and Subscription > Enterprise Subscription
desc: Onshape Enterprise is Onshape’s premium product offering designed for sophisticated product teams who need to work fast without losing control of data.

section: Managing Your Onshape Account and Subscription
title: Getting Started as an Enterprise User
path: Managing Your Onshape Account and Subscription > Enterprise Subscription > Getting Started as an Enterprise User
desc: When working within an Enterprise in Onshape, be aware that you are in a separate, managed environment that has a subtle difference from other types of Onshape subscriptions. The Enterprise environment is owned and managed by an Enterprise Administrator and can include many users, called Members of the Enterprise. All users belonging to a specific Enterprise plan access Onshape through a single URL, specifically for their Enterprise.

section: Managing Your Onshape Account and Subscription
title: Getting Started as a Light User
path: Managing Your Onshape Account and Subscription > Enterprise Subscription > Getting Started as a Light User
desc: Light user accounts are typically used by members of the internal supply chain, managers or executives, and can even be provided to external suppliers or clients. All Onshape users have access to the one single source of their enterprise data.

section: Managing Your Onshape Account and Subscription
title: Getting Started as an Enterprise Administrator
path: Managing Your Onshape Account and Subscription > Enterprise Subscription > Getting Started as an Enterprise Admin
desc: As an Enterprise Administrator, you are responsible for defining permissions for users. You have, by default, full access and full permission to your company’s resources. Optionally, you are able to grant similar permissions to other users using Global permissions.

section: Managing Your Onshape Account and Subscription
title: Two-factor Authentication for Enterprise
path: Managing Your Onshape Account and Subscription > Enterprise Subscription > Getting Started as an Enterprise Admin > Two-factor Authentication for Enterprise
desc: As the Admin of an Enterprise, you decide whether or not to require two-factor authentication use by company members. In the Company/Enterprise settings, you can configure your company's single sign-on and require two-factor authentication for Enterprise members.

section: Managing Your Onshape Account and Subscription
title: Project Roles and Permission Schemes
path: Managing Your Onshape Account and Subscription > Enterprise Subscription > Getting Started as an Enterprise Admin > Project Roles and Permission Schemes
desc: Project roles and Permission schemes work in tandem to apply access permission to documents grouped together within a Project. A Project references only one Permission scheme, which is comprised of Project roles specifying the permissions.

section: Managing Your Onshape Account and Subscription
title: Managing Projects
path: Managing Your Onshape Account and Subscription > Enterprise Subscription > Getting Started as an Enterprise Admin > Managing Projects
desc: Projects enable you to group documents and apply permissions to those documents for individual users and groups of users (called Teams). The permissions are assigned at the Project level through the association of a Permission scheme along with the specification of a role map (one per Project) that contains a list of user/role pairs. (The user may be an individual user or a Team of users.)

section: Managing Your Onshape Account and Subscription
title: Creating a Customized Release Workflow
path: Managing Your Onshape Account and Subscription > Enterprise Subscription > Getting Started as an Enterprise Admin > Creating a Customized Release Workflow
desc: Administrators of enterprises can create customized release and obsoletion workflows specific to the enterprise needs. Onshape provides a JSON file of our release and obsoletion workflows as a starting place for customizing the workflow to suit your company's needs. You can also use our JSON as a starting point for creating your own JSON file.

section: Managing Your Onshape Account and Subscription
title: Designing Release Management Processes
path: Managing Your Onshape Account and Subscription > Enterprise Subscription > Getting Started as an Enterprise Admin > Designing Release Management Processes
desc: Onshape provides generic release management workflows that you can start using immediately. This process is described in Typical Release Workflow. In addition to this generic workflow, Onshape provides you with the ability to design and create your own custom release management work flow, and then publish that workflow for your entire organization to use.

section: Managing Your Onshape Account and Subscription
title: Monitoring User Activity
path: Managing Your Onshape Account and Subscription > Enterprise Subscription > Monitoring User Activity
desc: Browse all Onshape activity of your Enterprise users from simple changes made to documents to viewing and responding to comments, and even viewing the differences (diffs) between versions of documents. If you are not an administrator of your company subscription, you see the activity of any document to which you have access.

section: Managing Your Onshape Account and Subscription
title: Monitoring Releases and Tasks
path: Managing Your Onshape Account and Subscription > Enterprise Subscription > Monitoring Releases and Tasks
desc: View and filter lists of releases and task activities on the Action items tab.

section: Managing Your Onshape Account and Subscription
title: Analytics
path: Managing Your Onshape Account and Subscription > Enterprise Subscription > Analytics
desc: Onshape provides dashboards for a variety of categories of information. Each user has access to all of the dashboards available to the enterprise, as long as they have been granted access to the Access analytics Global permission by the Enterprise administrator.

section: Managing Your Onshape Account and Subscription
title: Working with Analytics Dashboards
path: Managing Your Onshape Account and Subscription > Enterprise Subscription > Analytics > Working with Dashboards
desc: A dashboard is comprised of one or more visuals, and is the top level analytics page. All data is presented in dashboards with similar filtering, saving, report scheduling, editing, sharing, deleting, and exporting capabilities.

section: Managing Your Onshape Account and Subscription
title: Working with Analytics Dashboard Visuals
path: Managing Your Onshape Account and Subscription > Enterprise Subscription > Analytics > Working with Dashboard Visuals
desc: A dashboard visual is a dashboard component (sometimes referred to as a tile), consisting of a count, table, chart (bar, pie, donut), or map. Each dashboard can contain one or more visuals. Visuals have their own common set of controls. Visual data can be viewed, customized, added, removed, sorted, and exported.

section: Managing Your Onshape Account and Subscription
title: My Analytics Dashboards
path: Managing Your Onshape Account and Subscription > Enterprise Subscription > Analytics > My Analytics Dashboards
desc: The My analytics filter displays all your saved dashboards and any dashboards shared with you. You must have permissions to edit and save new dashboards, so they are displayed in this filter.

section: Managing Your Onshape Account and Subscription
title: Action Items Dashboards
path: Managing Your Onshape Account and Subscription > Enterprise Subscription > Analytics > Action Items Dashboards
desc: Action items dashboards summarize the comments and tasks for a specific user, and a summary for all users in an enterprise, in a specified time frame.

section: Managing Your Onshape Account and Subscription
title: Audit Dashboards
path: Managing Your Onshape Account and Subscription > Enterprise Subscription > Analytics > Audit Dashboards
desc: Audit dashboards summarize the events occurring on a specific document, or for a specific user, in a specified time frame.

section: Managing Your Onshape Account and Subscription
title: Documents Dashboards
path: Managing Your Onshape Account and Subscription > Enterprise Subscription > Analytics > Documents Dashboards
desc: Documents dashboards provide information about relationships between projects, users and documents, lists of documents available in the enterprise, and dashboards showing lists of permissions for a document or a user.

section: Managing Your Onshape Account and Subscription
title: Permission Dashboards
path: Managing Your Onshape Account and Subscription > Enterprise Subscription > Analytics > Permissions Dashboards
desc: Permissions dashboards provide information about permissions granted to users for a given document.

section: Managing Your Onshape Account and Subscription
title: Projects Dashboard
path: Managing Your Onshape Account and Subscription > Enterprise Subscription > Analytics > Projects Dashboard
desc: The Projects filter contains one Project list dashboard displaying all projects in the enterprise and their summary information.

section: Managing Your Onshape Account and Subscription
title: Release Dashboards
path: Managing Your Onshape Account and Subscription > Enterprise Subscription > Analytics > Release Dashboards
desc: Release dashboards provide both summary and detail information about release activity and contributors to the release process. Search for release candidates and parts.

section: Managing Your Onshape Account and Subscription
title: Resource Dashboards
path: Managing Your Onshape Account and Subscription > Enterprise Subscription > Analytics > Resource Dashboards
desc: Resource dashboards provide information on daily and detailed document and modeling activity.

section: Managing Your Onshape Account and Subscription
title: Users Dashboards
path: Managing Your Onshape Account and Subscription > Enterprise Subscription > Analytics > Users Dashboards
desc: Users dashboards list all users and teams in the enterprise, including members, administrators, and guests, and their summary information.

section: Managing Your Onshape Account and Subscription
title: Scheduled Reports
path: Managing Your Onshape Account and Subscription > Enterprise Subscription > Analytics > Scheduled Reports
desc: Enterprise and analytics Administrators can schedule reports of saved Onshape dashboards to be emailed to a list of recipients.

section: Managing Your Onshape Account and Subscription
title: Public Documents
path: Managing Your Onshape Account and Subscription > Enterprise Subscription > Public Documents
desc: Enterprise admins and users can access public documents once administrators give them the Allow access to public documents global permission. For users without rights to the Allow access to public documents permission, the enterprise domain prevents them from making enterprise data public or directly accessing public documents.

section: Managing Your Onshape Account and Subscription
title: Understanding Teams
path: Managing Your Onshape Account and Subscription > Enterprise Subscription > Understanding Teams
desc: Users need permission to create teams and assign other users to teams. Specifically, a user needs the Manage users and teams global permission in order to create teams and assign other users to a team. In Professional and Standard subscriptions, by contrast, anyone is able to create teams.

section: Managing Your Onshape Account and Subscription
title: Understanding Aliases
path: Managing Your Onshape Account and Subscription > Enterprise Subscription > Understanding Aliases
desc: Aliases are distribution lists for the Release management workflow. Only Administrators can create Aliases and assign other users or Teams to an alias. Specifically, an Administrator needs the Manage users and teams global permission in order to create aliases and assign other users or teams to an Alias.

section: Managing Your Onshape Account and Subscription
title: Onshape Government (US)
path: Managing Your Onshape Account and Subscription > Government (US) Subscription
desc: Onshape Government is a premium version of Onshape’s Enterprise subscription designed for teams that require a higher level of security and data protection, which also meets with governmental regulations and compliance. It is based on the same principles as the Onshape Enterprise subscription, with some key differences.

title: Contact Support / Contact Us
path: Contact Support / Contact Us
desc: If you have specific CAD-related questions with regard to using Onshape, you always have the ability to look through questions and answers within the greater Onshape Community via our Forums. If you can't find a relevant answer to your question in the Forums, feel free to submit a support ticket.

title: Glossary
path: Glossary
desc: Onshape glossary, providing definitions for key Onshape software terms. Covers terms in the context of Documents, Sketches, Part Studios, Assemblies, Drawings, Render Studios, and Accounts, as well as all plan types.

title: Icon Glossary
path: Icon Glossary
desc: A glossary of Onshape icons categorized by General, Tab type, and Document rows. The tables in each row provide Button names and actions, and indicator descriptions.
